\subsection{A sufficient kernel criterion for positive tail jets}
\label{subsec:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel}

We now separate the kernel properties from their stable implementation.  The
following is a sufficient kernel criterion; no necessity or global
minimality assertion is made.  Fix an integer \(r\ge1\).  A strictly positive
probability density \(p\in C^r(\RR^d)\) will be called \emph{tail-jet
admissible of order \(r\)} if the following two conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(K\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item For every multi-index \(\gamma\) with \(1\le|\gamma|\le r\),
\[
 \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty<\infty.
\]
\item The top normalized derivative has quotient translation modulus
\[
 \omega_{p,r}(t):=
 \max_{|\gamma|=r}\ \sup_{|h|\le t}
 \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)
                   -\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty,
 \qquad 0<t\le1,
\]
and \(\omega_{p,r}(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
\end{enumerate}
The omitted finiteness clause is automatic.  Indeed, if
\(M_r=\max_{|\gamma|=r}\|\partial^\gamma p/p\|_\infty\) and
\(L=\|\nabla\log p\|_\infty\), then, for \(|h|\le1\),
\[
 \frac{|\partial^\gamma p(y-h)-\partial^\gamma p(y)|}{p(y)}
 \le M_r\{e^{L|h|}+1\}.
\]

\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Zero mass of integrable density derivatives]
If \(p\in C^r(\RR^d)\) and \(\partial^\gamma p\in L^1\) for
\(|\gamma|\le r\), then
\[
 \int_{\RR^d}\partial^\gamma p(y)\dd y=0,
 \qquad 1\le|\gamma|\le r.
\]
\end{unnumberedlemma}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(j\) with \(\gamma_j>0\), put
\(f=\partial^{\gamma-e_j}p\in W^{1,1}\), and test
\(\partial_jf\) against cutoffs \(\chi_R\to1\) with
\(\|\nabla\chi_R\|_\infty=O(R^{-1})\).  Then
\(\int\chi_R\partial_jf=-\int f\partial_j\chi_R\to0\), while dominated
convergence sends the left side to \(\int\partial_jf\).
\end{proof}

\begin{unnumberedlemma}[Bounded-score translate entropy]
If \(p>0\), \(p\in C^1(\RR^d)\), and
\(\|\nabla\log p\|_\infty\le L\), then, for every \(z\in\RR^d\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bounded-score-translate-entropy}
 0\le D_{\rm KL}\bigl(p(\mathord\cdot-z)\|p\bigr)\le L|z|.
\end{equation}
\end{unnumberedlemma}

\begin{proof}
After the change of variables \(w=y-z\), the divergence is
\(\int p(w)\log\{p(w)/p(w+z)\}\dd w\).  The fundamental theorem of
calculus bounds the absolute value of the logarithm by \(L|z|\); integration
and nonnegativity of relative entropy give
\eqref{eq:bounded-score-translate-entropy}.
\end{proof}

Put \(p_s(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)\),
\(\Omega_p(\dd y)=p(y)\dd y\), and
\[
 F_y^p(z)=\frac{p(y-z)}{p(y)}.
\]
For a law \(\lambda\) with finite \(r\)th absolute moment define
\[
 B_{p,j}^\lambda(y):=
 \frac{(-1)^j}{p(y)}
 \sum_{|\gamma|=j}\frac{m_\gamma(\lambda)}{\gamma!}
 \partial^\gamma p(y),\qquad 1\le j\le r.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Abstract positive tail-jet kernel theorem]
\label{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel}
Let \(p\) be tail-jet admissible of order \(r\), and let \(\nu,\eta\) be
probability laws on \(\RR^d\) such that
\[
 m_\gamma(\nu)=m_\gamma(\eta)\quad(|\gamma|<r),
 \qquad \int |x|^r(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
\]
For \(\lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\}\), set
\[
 \tau_s^\lambda=\lambda(|x|>s),\qquad
 V_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=
 \int_{|x|>s}F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),
\]
and let the common retained jet and the two proxies be
\begin{align*}
 C_{p,r-1,s}
 &=\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\nu
  =\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\eta,\\
 A_{p,s}^\lambda
 &=1+C_{p,r-1,s}+V_{p,s}^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda.
\end{align*}
The sum is empty when \(r=1\).  For all sufficiently large \(s\), both
\(A_{p,s}^\lambda\) are positive probability densities relative to
\(\Omega_p\).  Thus
\[
 k_{p,r,s}^\lambda(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)A_{p,s}^\lambda(x/s)
\]
are probability densities and the finite, nonnegative proxy energy
\[
 \mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
 :=D_{\rm KL}(k_{p,r,s}^\nu\|k_{p,r,s}^\eta)
\]
is well defined.  If
\(\Delta_r=\int x^{\otimes r}(\nu-\eta)(\dd x)\), put
\[
 B_{p,\Delta_r}(y)=
 \frac{(-1)^r}{r!p(y)}\langle\Delta_r,D^rp(y)\rangle,
 \qquad
 \mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
 =\frac12\int B_{p,\Delta_r}^2\dd\Omega_p.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-tail-defect-decomposition}
 D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
 =\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
  +\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
\end{equation}
Moreover \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) is finite and positive definite on
\(\operatorname{Sym}^r(\RR^d)\), and hence, law by law,
\[
 s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
 \longrightarrow\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 s^{2r}\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let
\[
 \mathsf B_{p,j}(y,z)=
 \frac{(-1)^j}{j!p(y)}\langle D^jp(y),z^{\otimes j}\rangle,
 \qquad \mathsf B_{p,0}=1.
\]
Condition \textup{(K1)} gives, for \(1\le j\le r\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-tail-mode-bounds}
 \|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_\infty
 +\|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}
 \le C_{p,r}|z|^j.
\end{equation}
It also puts every derivative through order \(r\) in \(L^1\), so the
zero-mass lemma applies.  Ordinary translation continuity in \(L^1\), the
integral Taylor formula, and \textup{(K2)} imply that, for \(|z|\le1\),
\begin{align}
 &\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_\infty
 +\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}\notag\\
 &\hspace{35mm}\le \varepsilon_{p,r}(|z|)|z|^r,
 \label{eq:abstract-tail-local-remainder}
\end{align}
where \(\varepsilon_{p,r}\) is bounded on \([0,1]\) and tends to zero at
zero.  The uniform remainder is bounded by a constant times
\(|z|^r\omega_{p,r}(|z|)\).  After multiplication by \(p(y)\), the
\(L^1(\Omega_p)\) remainder is bounded by a constant times
\[
 |z|^r\max_{|\gamma|=r}\sup_{|h|\le|z|}
 \|\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)-\partial^\gamma p\|_1,
\]
which is \(o(|z|^r)\).  Thus only \(C^r\), not \(C^{r+1}\), is used.

Define the actual quotient
\[
 q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=\int F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
\]
Splitting at \(|x|=s\), retaining the exterior translate exactly, and using
the moments gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-tail-exact-quotient-split}
 q_{p,s}^\lambda
 =A_{p,s}^\lambda+s^{-r}B_{p,r}^\lambda+R_{p,s}^\lambda,
 \qquad
 \|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_\infty
 +\|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}=o(s^{-r}).
\end{equation}
After multiplication by \(s^r\), the interior Taylor remainder is dominated
by \(C|x|^r\) and converges pointwise to zero.  Every discarded exterior
mode satisfies
\[
 s^{-j}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^j\lambda(\dd x)
 \le s^{-r}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)=o(s^{-r}),
 \qquad j\le r,
\]
and the same estimate gives \(\tau_s^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).

Translation preserves mass, so \(V_{p,s}^\lambda\ge0\) and
\(\int V_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=\tau_s^\lambda\).  The zero-mass lemma
gives \(\int B_{p,j}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=0\).  Therefore each proxy has mass
one, and
\[
 \inf_yA_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
 \ge1-\|C_{p,r-1,s}\|_\infty-\tau_s^\lambda\longrightarrow1.
\]
This proves normalization and positivity without a tail comparison.

We next verify entropy finiteness using only \textup{(K1)}.  Put
\(L=\|\nabla\log p\|_\infty\).  When \(\tau_s^\lambda>0\), convexity of
relative entropy and the bounded-score entropy lemma give, for
\(Q_{p,s}^\lambda=V_{p,s}^\lambda/\tau_s^\lambda\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}
 \int Q_{p,s}^\lambda\log Q_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p
 \le\frac{L}{s\tau_s^\lambda}
 \int_{|x|>s}|x|\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
\end{equation}
The first moment is finite because \(r\ge1\).  The inequalities
\(\Phi(\tau q)\le\tau q\log(1+q)\) for \(0\le\tau\le1\), and
\[
 (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
 \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
\]
then show
\(\int A_{p,s}^\lambda\log^+A_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p<\infty\).
The case \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\) is immediate.  Since the two proxies have a
common positive lower bound, their relative entropy is finite.

The bounded score also gives
\[
 F_y^p(z)\ge e^{-L|z|},\qquad
 q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
 \ge e^{-L\int|x|\lambda(\dd x)/s}\longrightarrow1
\]
uniformly in \(y\).  The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1(\Omega_p)\), and
their common jet cancels, so
\begin{align*}
 \|A_{p,s}^\lambda-1\|_1
 &\le\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_{p,j}^\lambda\|_1
      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1),\\
 \|A_{p,s}^\nu-A_{p,s}^\eta\|_1
 &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
\end{align*}
All hypotheses of the two-background KL perturbation lemma are satisfied
with \(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\).  Its Hessian and cubic-remainder calculation
gives
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
 =\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
  +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int
       (B_{p,r}^\nu-B_{p,r}^\eta)^2\dd\Omega_p+o(s^{-2r}).
\]
The moment identity makes the difference in the integral exactly
\(B_{p,\Delta_r}\), proving \eqref{eq:abstract-tail-defect-decomposition}.

Finiteness of \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) follows from \textup{(K1)}.  If it
vanishes, then
\[
 \sum_{|\gamma|=r}\frac{\Delta m_\gamma}{\gamma!}
 \partial^\gamma p=0
\]
almost everywhere.  Fourier transformation gives
\(P(i\xi)\widehat p(\xi)=0\), where \(P\) is the corresponding homogeneous
polynomial.  Since \(\widehat p(0)=1\), continuity makes \(\widehat p\)
nonzero on a neighborhood of zero.  Thus \(P\) vanishes on an open set and
is identically zero.  Hence \(\Delta_r=0\), proving positive definiteness.
Nonnegativity of the proxy KL energy proves the final equivalence.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Closure and verified kernel classes]
\label{prop:tail-jet-kernel-closure-and-examples}
For each fixed order \(r\), tail-jet admissibility is preserved by:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item invertible affine images;
\item finite tensor products, allowing different block dimensions; and
\item finite positive mixtures of admissible densities on the same space.
\end{enumerate}
The criterion of Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel}
therefore applies to every kernel obtained by finitely combining these
operations.  Its base members include, at every order, each isotropic
strictly \(\alpha\)-stable density, \(0<\alpha<2\), the Poisson kernel in
every dimension, and every multivariate Student kernel
\[
 p_{\beta,d}(y)=c_{\beta,d}(1+|y|^2)^{-\beta/2},\qquad \beta>d.
\]
In particular, affine mixtures and products of these kernels give generally
nonradial, nonstable members of the criterion.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Write \(R_{p,\gamma}=\partial^\gamma p/p\).  Under \textup{(K1)}, every
\(R_{p,\gamma}\) with \(|\gamma|<r\) is globally Lipschitz, since
\[
 \partial_jR_{p,\gamma}
 =R_{p,\gamma+e_j}-R_{p,\gamma}R_{p,e_j}.
\]
For \(|\gamma|=r\), \textup{(K2)} and the bounded score imply uniform
continuity of \(R_{p,\gamma}\): for \(|h|\le t\),
\[
 |R_{p,\gamma}(y-h)-R_{p,\gamma}(y)|
 \le\omega_{p,r}(t)+\|R_{p,\gamma}\|_\infty(e^{Lt}-1).
\]
Conversely, uniform continuity of the bounded top normalized derivatives,
together with \(p(y-h)/p(y)\in[e^{-L|h|},e^{L|h|}]\), implies
\textup{(K2)}.  We use this equivalent form for products.

If \(q(x)=|\det A|^{-1}p(A^{-1}(x-b))\), the chain rule expresses every
normalized derivative of \(q\) as a fixed linear combination of normalized
derivatives of \(p\).  A translation by \(h\) for \(q\) becomes a
translation by \(A^{-1}h\) for \(p\).  This proves affine closure.

For a product \(q(x_1,\ldots,x_N)=\prod_{i=1}^Np_i(x_i)\), a block
multi-index \(\gamma=(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_N)\) satisfies
\[
 R_{q,\gamma}(x)=\prod_{i=1}^N R_{p_i,\gamma_i}(x_i),
 \qquad R_{p_i,0}=1.
\]
These factors are bounded and uniformly continuous: they are Lipschitz below
order \(r\), and the preceding equivalence handles order \(r\).  Hence the
product satisfies \textup{(K1)} and \textup{(K2)}.

Finally let \(q=\sum_{i=1}^Na_ip_i\), where \(a_i>0\) and
\(\sum_i a_i=1\).  With \(w_i(y)=a_ip_i(y)/q(y)\),
\[
 R_{q,\gamma}(y)=\sum_iw_i(y)R_{p_i,\gamma}(y),
 \qquad \sum_iw_i(y)=1,
\]
so \textup{(K1)} follows.  Moreover,
\[
 \omega_{q,r}(t)
 \le\max_i\omega_{p_i,r}(t)\longrightarrow0,
\]
which proves mixture closure.

For isotropic stable kernels, Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}
gives, with \(\beta=d+\alpha\),
\[
 p(y)\asymp(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
 |\partial^\gamma p(y)|\le C_\gamma
 (1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\gamma|}.
\]
This proves \textup{(K1)}.  The bound one order higher, the mean-value
theorem, and \(1+|y|\le2(1+|y-th|)\) give
\(\omega_{p,r}(t)\le Ct\), proving \textup{(K2)}.  The bounded-score lemma
then supplies translate entropy without an additional hypothesis.  The
stable notation is identified explicitly in
Corollary~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition} below.

At unit height the Poisson kernel is the Student member
\(P_1^{(d)}(y)=c_d(1+|y|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}\).  For general \(\beta>d\), repeated
differentiation shows that every
\(\partial^\gamma p_{\beta,d}/p_{\beta,d}\) is a finite sum of terms
\[
 c_{\gamma,k}\frac{y^{\delta_{\gamma,k}}}{(1+|y|^2)^k},
 \qquad |\delta_{\gamma,k}|\le2k,
\]
and is bounded.  The same statement one order higher, together with
\(p_{\beta,d}(y-th)/p_{\beta,d}(y)\le C_{\beta,d}\) for \(|h|\le1\), gives
\(\omega_{p,r}(t)\le Ct\).  Thus the Student and Poisson kernels satisfy
\textup{(K1)}--\textup{(K2)}, completing the verification.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Gaussian mechanism boundary]
\label{prop:gaussian-additive-proxy-mechanism-boundary}
The standard Gaussian is not tail-jet admissible at any order.  More
strongly, at order two there are moment-matched inputs for which the
prescribed additive common-jet proxies are negative.  Thus
Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel} describes the
bounded-score/additive branch of the proxy geometry.  Gaussian smoothing
belongs to a different, unbounded-score/multiplicative or exponential-score
branch requiring weighted Hermite control; this proposition is a mechanism
boundary, not a theorem covering Gaussian smoothing.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For the standard Gaussian \(g\),
\[
 \partial^\gamma g/g=(-1)^{|\gamma|}H_\gamma,
 \qquad \nabla\log g(y)=-y,
\]
so \textup{(K1)} fails already at first order.  The quotient
\[
 F_y^g(z)=\exp\{y\mathbin\cdot z-|z|^2/2\}
\]
has infimum zero for every \(z\ne0\), and the corresponding difference
quotients in \textup{(K2)} are unbounded for every nonzero translation.
Hence the uniform lower background used by the additive two-background
expansion is unavailable.

The proxy failure is explicit in dimension one at \(r=2\).  Take
\(\nu=\delta_m\) and
\(\eta=(\delta_{m-a}+\delta_{m+a})/2\), where \(m\ne0\) and \(a>0\).
They have the same mass and first moment.  For \(s>|m|+a\), the retained
tails vanish, while the common first Gaussian mode is \(my\); both
prescribed proxies therefore equal \(1+my/s\), which is negative on a
half-line.  Consequently, the uniformly bounded cubic-remainder estimate in
the two-background additive-jet expansion is unavailable.  Gaussian
translate entropy is not the obstruction at orders \(r\ge2\), since
\(D_{\rm KL}(g(\mathord\cdot-z)\|g)=|z|^2/2\).  Weighted Hermite arguments
can prove Gaussian first-unmatched-moment asymptotics under stronger input
hypotheses, but they use the different proxy geometry stated above.
\end{proof}

Assume throughout the hypotheses and notation of
Corollary~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  For
\(\lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\}\), let
\(\chi^\lambda=(\chi_s^\lambda)_{s>0}\).  Call
\((\boldsymbol\chi,H)=((\chi^\nu,\chi^\eta),H)\) an admissible fixed-scale
tail-jet convention if there are common constants
\(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\) and \(\lambda\), such that
\[
 0\le\chi_s^\lambda\le1,\qquad
 \chi_s^\lambda(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
 \chi_s^\lambda(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
\]
where every \(\chi_s^\lambda:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
\[
 \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
 \qquad

        \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
\]
The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  No relation between

inner and outer radii.

\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
the corresponding additively normalized proxy with \(H=0\) satisfies
\[
 \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
 \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
 \qquad
 A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
\]
Consequently,
\[
 A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
 =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
 \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
 \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
\]
The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
 =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
   +o(s^{-2r}),
\]
whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
actual smoothed entropy coefficient
\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
class boundary is not a proof artifact.

\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
Define, for \(\lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\}\),
\begin{align*}
 \tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda
  &:=\int\chi_s^\lambda(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
 V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda(y)
  &:=\int\chi_s^\lambda(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
 A_s^{\lambda;\boldsymbol\chi,H}
  &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda-
       \tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s,\\
 \widetilde A_s^{\lambda;\boldsymbol\chi,H}
  &:=\frac{1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s}
          {1+\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda}.
\end{align*}
These are, respectively, the additive and multiplicative mass
normalizations.  For all sufficiently large \(s\), both pairs are positive
probability densities relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\).  Their relative
entropies
\[
 \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
 :=\int A_s^{\eta;\boldsymbol\chi,H}
 \Phi\!\left(
  \frac{A_s^{\nu;\boldsymbol\chi,H}
        -A_s^{\eta;\boldsymbol\chi,H}}
       {A_s^{\eta;\boldsymbol\chi,H}}
 \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d},
\]
and
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal E}_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
 :=D_{\rm KL}(\widetilde A_s^{\nu;\boldsymbol\chi,H}
              \|\widetilde A_s^{\eta;\boldsymbol\chi,H})
\]
are finite and satisfy
\[
 \left|\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
       -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
 =o(s^{-2r}).
\]
For either normalization, writing its energy as
\(\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\mathrm{norm}}\), one has
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\mathrm{norm}}(\nu,\eta)
  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
\]
Consequently, the energies of any two admissible fixed-scale conventions,
with either of these two mass normalizations in either convention, differ by
\(o(s^{-2r})\).  In particular, the truth of the condition
\[
 s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\mathrm{norm}}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0
\]
is independent of the convention and of these two normalization choices,
as is the Hessian constant \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).

The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
\(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
\(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
\(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
\(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
No assertion is made for proxy constructions outside this prescribed
fixed-smoothing-scale tail/core class or for normalization rules other than
the two displayed above.
\end{unnumberedproposition}

\begin{proof}
Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
of Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel}, and put
\(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
\[
 q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\boldsymbol\chi,H}
  +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda,
\]
where
\begin{align*}
 R_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda
 &=\int(1-\chi_s^\lambda(x/s))
   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
 &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s^\lambda(x/s)
                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
\end{align*}
On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
used in \eqref{eq:abstract-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
\(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since
\(1-\chi_s^\lambda(x/s)\)
vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:abstract-tail-mode-bounds} give
\[
 \left\|\int\chi_s^\lambda(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
 +\left\|\int\chi_s^\lambda(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
             \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
 \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
\]
It follows that
\[
 \|R_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\|_\infty+
 \|R_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
\]
The same tail estimate yields
\(\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).

Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
\(V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\ge0\),
\(\int V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
=\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
mean.  Moreover,
\[
 \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\boldsymbol\chi,H}(y)
 \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
       \tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
\]
The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
\eqref{eq:abstract-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
\(\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives,
for \(Q_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda
=V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\),
\[
 \int Q_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda
       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda}
 \int\chi_s^\lambda(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
              \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
\]
The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
\(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite
positive entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda=0\) is
immediate.

Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
\[
 A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\boldsymbol\chi,H},\quad
 A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\boldsymbol\chi,H},\quad
 B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
\]
The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
gauge cancel, so
\[
 \|A_s^{\nu;\boldsymbol\chi,H}
       -A_s^{\eta;\boldsymbol\chi,H}\|_1
 \le2(\tau_{s,\chi^\nu}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi^\eta}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
\]
All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
\((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
Subtracting the expansions for two additive conventions proves their
\(o(s^{-2r})\) equivalence.

It remains to compare the two normalizations.  Put \(\epsilon=s^{-r}\),
write \(A_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\boldsymbol\chi,H}\) and
\(\tau_s^\lambda=\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\), and interpolate by
\[
 X_{s,\theta}^\lambda
 :=\frac{A_s^\lambda+\theta\tau_s^\lambda}
         {1+\theta\tau_s^\lambda},\qquad 0\le\theta\le1.
\]
Thus \(X_{s,0}^\lambda=A_s^\lambda\) and
\(X_{s,1}^\lambda=\widetilde A_s^\lambda\).  We first record the entropy
estimate that replaces an unavailable \(L^\infty\) bound on the retained
potential.  The preceding mixture bound, the bounded negative part of
\(q\log q\), and \(\log(1+u)\le C_{a,r}u^r\) for \(u\ge a\) give
\begin{align*}
 \int V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda
       \log^+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 &\le C\tau_s^\lambda
   +C\int\chi_s^\lambda(x/s)
          \{1+\log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
 &\le C\tau_s^\lambda
   +Cs^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)
 =o(\epsilon).
\end{align*}
For fixed \(0<c<C<\infty\), the elementary pointwise bound
\[
 h(b+u,b'+v)\le C_{c,C}
 \{(b-b')^2+u+v+u\log^+u+v\log^+v\},
 \quad h(x,y)=x\log(x/y)-x+y,
\]
holds for \(c\le b,b'\le C\) and \(u,v\ge0\).  To see this, use the
quadratic Taylor bound for \(h\) when \(u+v\le1\); when \(u+v>1\), absorb
the constant in \(u+v\) and use the defining formula for \(h\).
The bounded cores of \(X_{s,\theta}^\nu\) and
\(X_{s,\theta}^\eta\) differ by
\(O(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(\epsilon)\), uniformly in \(\theta\), while
their nonnegative retained parts obey the last display.  Consequently,
uniformly for \(0\le\theta\le1\),
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(X_{s,\theta}^\nu\|X_{s,\theta}^\eta)=o(\epsilon),
 \qquad
 \|X_{s,\theta}^\nu-X_{s,\theta}^\eta\|_1=o(\epsilon).
\]

Let \(K_s(\theta)=D_{\rm KL}(X_{s,\theta}^\nu
\|X_{s,\theta}^\eta)\) and
\(a_s^\lambda(\theta)=\tau_s^\lambda/(1+\theta\tau_s^\lambda)\).
Since
\(\partial_\theta X_{s,\theta}^\lambda
=a_s^\lambda(\theta)(1-X_{s,\theta}^\lambda)\), differentiation gives
\begin{align*}
 K_s'(\theta)
 &=a_s^\nu(\theta)\int(1-X_{s,\theta}^\nu)
       \log\frac{X_{s,\theta}^\nu}{X_{s,\theta}^\eta}
       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\\
 &\quad-a_s^\eta(\theta)\int
       \frac{(X_{s,\theta}^\nu-X_{s,\theta}^\eta)
             (1-X_{s,\theta}^\eta)}{X_{s,\theta}^\eta}
       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}.
\end{align*}
The second integral is \(o(\epsilon)\), because all interpolants have a
common positive lower bound and \(|1-y|/y\) is bounded there.  For the first
integral, use
\[
 \int(1-x)\log(x/y)\dd\Omega
 =\int\log(x/y)\dd\Omega-D_{\rm KL}(x\|y),
 \qquad
 \int|\log(x/y)|\dd\Omega\le c^{-1}\|x-y\|_1.
\]
It too is \(o(\epsilon)\).  Since
\(a_s^\lambda(\theta)=o(\epsilon)\), uniformly in \(\theta\), we obtain
\(\sup_{0\le\theta\le1}|K_s'(\theta)|=o(\epsilon^2)\).
The preceding finite-entropy estimates justify the differentiation; one may
equivalently truncate the retained potentials and pass to the limit using
the displayed integrable bounds.  Integration from zero to one proves
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal E}_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}
 -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}=o(s^{-2r}).
\]
Combining this with the additive expansion proves all remaining assertions.
\end{proof}

\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Asymptotic coefficient rigidity inside a prescribed ansatz]
Fix an admissible pair \(\boldsymbol\chi=(\chi^\nu,\chi^\eta)\).  Consider
positive normalized
proxies of the form
\[
 \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda-
                         \tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda,
 \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
\]
where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
\(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
\(S_s^\lambda\) such that
\[
 q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
 \qquad
 \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
\]
Then
\[
 H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
\]
is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
\[
 \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
 +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
\]
In particular,
\[
 \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
 +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
\]
Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
one initially writes the normalized proxy as
\(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar
counterterm, then normalization forces
\(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\) exactly.
\end{unnumberedproposition}

\begin{proof}
The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
terms agree, subtraction gives
\[
 s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
   =s^r(R_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
\]
The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
\(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
\(H_s\), and
\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Scope of the coefficient-rigidity statement.}
This is asymptotic coefficient rigidity inside the prescribed ansatz.  The
result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
it is not a uniqueness, canonicity, or entropy-minimality theorem for all
positive proxy constructions.

\begin{lemma}[Uniform Bernoulli relative-entropy separation]
\label{lem:bernoulli-kl-linear-separation}
Let \(0<b<a\).  If \(u\ge aw\) and \(v\le bw\) are Bernoulli parameters,
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bernoulli-kl-linear-separation}
 D_{\rm KL}(\operatorname{Ber}(u)\|\operatorname{Ber}(v))
 \ge a\left\{\log\frac ab-1+\frac ba\right\}w.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If \(v=0<u\), the relative entropy is infinite.  Otherwise \(u>v>0\), and
\[
 (1-u)\log\frac{1-u}{1-v}\ge-(u-v).
\]
Writing \(\theta=v/u\le b/a<1\) therefore gives
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(\operatorname{Ber}(u)\|\operatorname{Ber}(v))
 \ge u\{\log(1/\theta)-1+\theta\}
 \ge aw\left\{\log\frac ab-1+\frac ba\right\},
\]
because the braced function is decreasing on \((0,1)\).
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Gaussian benchmark and priority.}
Let \(\rho_t(x)=(2\pi t)^{-d/2}e^{-|x|^2/(2t)}\).  Under a finite
exponential square moment for each centred input, Chen and Niles-Weed
\cite[Theorem~2.5]{ChenNilesWeed2022SmoothedWasserstein} prove that moment
matching below order \(r=n+1\), followed by a nonzero difference at order
\(r\), implies, with
\(\Delta m_\gamma=m_\gamma(\mu)-m_\gamma(\eta)\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:chen-niles-weed-gaussian-kl-benchmark}
 \lim_{t\to\infty}t^rD_{\rm KL}(\mu*\rho_t\|\eta*\rho_t)
 =\frac12\sum_{|\gamma|=r}\frac{|\Delta m_\gamma|^2}{\gamma!}.
\end{equation}
Putting \(s=\sqrt t\) gives the same \(s^{-2r}\) scaling as below.  For the
standard Gaussian \(g=\rho_1\), the identities
\((-1)^{|\gamma|}\partial^\gamma g=H_\gamma g\) and
\(\int H_\gamma H_\delta g=\gamma!\mathbf1_{\gamma=\delta}\) identify the
right side of \eqref{eq:chen-niles-weed-gaussian-kl-benchmark} exactly with
the quadratic functional \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-leading-functional} at
the Gaussian boundary \(\alpha=2\).  Accordingly, the first-unmatched
quadratic KL mechanism and its positivity are prior work in the Gaussian
case.  The theorem below contributes the heavy-tailed range \(0<\alpha<2\),
the critical complete-moment exponent, endpoint sufficiency, and uniform
sharpness over those moment classes.

\begin{theorem}[All-order first unmatched tensor under stable smoothing]
\label{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment}
Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), and let \(r\ge1\) be an integer.  Define
\(q_{r,\alpha,d}\) and \(p_{r,\alpha,d}\) by
\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-critical-exponents}.  Let \(\nu,\eta\) be
probability laws on \(\RR^d\) such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:all-order-stable-moment-hypotheses}
 m_\gamma(\nu)=m_\gamma(\eta)\quad(|\gamma|<r),
 \qquad
 \int|x|^{p_{r,\alpha,d}}(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
\end{equation}
Put
\[
 \Delta_r:=\int_{\RR^d}x^{\otimes r}(\nu-\eta)(\dd x)
 \in\operatorname{Sym}^r(\RR^d),
\]
so its multi-index coordinates are
\(\Delta m_\gamma=m_\gamma(\nu)-m_\gamma(\eta)\), and suppose
\(\Delta_r\ne0\).  With the Euclidean contraction of symmetric tensors,
define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:all-order-stable-leading-mode}
 B_{\Delta_r}(y):=
 \frac{(-1)^r}{r!p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)}
 \langle\Delta_r,D^rp_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\rangle
 =\frac{(-1)^r}{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)}
 \sum_{|\gamma|=r}\frac{\Delta m_\gamma}{\gamma!}
 \partial^\gamma p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:all-order-stable-leading-functional}
 \mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
 :=\frac12\int_{\RR^d}B_{\Delta_r}(y)^2
                  \Omega_{\alpha,d}(\dd y).
\end{equation}
Then \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)>0\), the quadratic form is
invariant under \(\Delta_r\mapsto U^{\otimes r}\Delta_r\) for every
\(U\in O(d)\), and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-asymptotic}
 D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
\end{equation}

The exponent \(p_{r,\alpha,d}\) is optimal as a uniform sufficient
absolute-moment hypothesis, with its endpoint included.  More precisely,
if \(d+\alpha>2r\), then for every
\(r\le\rho<p_{r,\alpha,d}\) there are probability laws \(\nu,\eta\)
having finite \(\rho\)th absolute moments, matching every tensor moment
below order \(r\), and having a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference,
but
\begin{equation}\label{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}
 \limsup_{s\to\infty}s^{2r}
 D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)=+\infty.
\end{equation}
For \(0<\rho<r\), finiteness of the \(\rho\)th absolute moment does not
even guarantee that the tensor in \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-leading-mode}
is defined throughout the moment class.  Thus the latter observation is a
domain obstruction, whereas \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness} is the
analytic sharpness statement on laws for which the leading tensor exists.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write \(q=q_{r,\alpha,d}\), \(p=p_{r,\alpha,d}\), and
\(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  Apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:all-order-stable-critical-remainder} to both laws.  Their
common moments below order \(r\) cancel, so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:all-order-stable-two-quotient-split}
 q_s^\nu-q_s^\eta=v_s+e_s,
 \quad
 v_s=\sum_{j=r}^m s^{-j}(B_j^\nu-B_j^\eta),
 \quad
 e_s=r_s^\nu-r_s^\eta.
\end{equation}
In particular,
\[
 s^rv_s\longrightarrow B_{\Delta_r}\quad\hbox{in }L^\infty,
 \qquad \|e_s\|_q=o(s^{-p}).
\]
The intermediate modes \(r<j\le m\) in
\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-two-quotient-split} are essential: unless their
moments also match, they are not part of the \(o(s^{-p})\) remainder.

No part of this argument requires \(r\ge2\).  At \(r=1\), the endpoint
formula still gives \(p\ge1\), hence the assumed \(p\)-moment supplies the
first moments and \(\EE|X|<\infty\); also \(m+1>p\) and \(pq=2\).  Thus the
critical remainder and the two-background transfer have exactly the powers
needed for an \(o(s^{-2})\) error.  Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}
records the corresponding first-difference block used for sharpness.

Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} implies
\(\|\nabla\log p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\|_\infty\le L_{\alpha,d}\).  Hence, if
\(X\) has law \(\lambda\),
\[
 q_s^\lambda(y)
 \ge\EE\exp(-L_{\alpha,d}|X|/s)
 \ge\exp(-L_{\alpha,d}\EE|X|/s),
\]
uniformly in \(y\).  The last expression tends to one.  Translation
continuity of \(p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\) in \(L^1\) gives, by Tonelli and dominated
convergence,
\[
 \|q_s^\eta-1\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
 \le\int\|p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(\mathord\cdot-x/s)
              -p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\|_1\,\eta(\dd x)\longrightarrow0;
\]
the integrand is bounded by two.  A second Tonelli calculation gives
\(\int q_s^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=1\) for every probability law
\(\lambda\).  These are precisely the positive lower bound, mass
normalization, and \(L^1\)-convergence required of the denominator by
Lemma~\ref{lem:two-background-critical-bregman-transfer}; no
\(L^\infty\)-convergence of \(q_s^\eta\) to one is used.  Taking
\(g_s=q_s^\eta\) in that lemma proves
\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-asymptotic}.

Boundedness of \(B_{\Delta_r}\) makes
\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}\) finite.  If it were zero, then
\[
 \sum_{|\gamma|=r}\frac{\Delta m_\gamma}{\gamma!}
 \partial^\gamma p_1^{(\alpha,d)}=0
\]
almost everywhere.  Fourier transformation in the sense of tempered
distributions gives a homogeneous polynomial in \(\xi\), with coefficients
\(\Delta m_\gamma/\gamma!\), multiplied by the nowhere-vanishing stable
characteristic function.  The polynomial must vanish identically, contrary
to \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  This proves strict positivity.  If \(U\in O(d)\),
isotropy and the tensor chain rule give
\(B_{U^{\otimes r}\Delta_r}(Uy)=B_{\Delta_r}(y)\).  Orthogonal invariance of
\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\) then proves the asserted invariance of \(\mathcal Q\).
For \(d\ge2\), under the homogeneous-polynomial identification, the standard
trace/harmonic decomposition
\[
 \operatorname{Sym}^r(\RR^d)
 =\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\lfloor r/2\rfloor}
   |x|^{2k}\mathcal H_{r-2k}
\]
is multiplicity-free under \(O(d)\).  Hence the self-adjoint operator of
\(\mathcal Q\) is scalar on each harmonic summand; the positivity just proved
shows that all these scalars are strictly positive.  No formula for the
individual scalars is needed below.

It remains to establish sharpness.  Assume \(\beta=d+\alpha>2r\), so
\[
 q=1+\frac{2r}{\beta},\qquad p=\frac{2r}{q}>r.
\]
Fix a unit vector \(e\), and let \(A_R^\pm\) be the probability blocks from
Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}.

Choose \(a_j>0\) with \(\sum_ja_j<\infty\).  Choose the radii recursively so
that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:all-order-separated-block-radii}
 R_{j+1}>4(r+1)R_j,
\end{equation}
and enlarge each new radius further whenever necessary below.  Put
\(w_j=a_jR_j^{-\rho}\), with \(\sum_jw_j<1\), and define
\[
 \nu=\left(1-\sum_jw_j\right)\delta_0+\sum_jw_jA_{R_j}^+,
 \qquad
 \eta=\left(1-\sum_jw_j\right)\delta_0+\sum_jw_jA_{R_j}^-.
\]
They have finite \(\rho\)th moments.  Since \(\rho\ge r\),
\eqref{eq:stable-block-moment-identities} also shows that their
order-\(r\) tensor difference is finite and nonzero.

The endpoint \(x_j=(r+1)R_je\) belongs to \(A_{R_j}^+\) and not to
\(A_{R_j}^-\).  Let \(E_j\) be the ball of radius
\[
 s_j=\kappa R_jw_j^{1/\beta}
\]
about \(x_j\).  Recursive enlargement of \(R_j\) makes \(s_j\to\infty\);
also \(s_j/R_j=\kappa w_j^{1/\beta}<1/4\) for all sufficiently large \(j\).
Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-moving-ball-probability-separation} gives both
probability bounds, after explicitly separating \(E_j\) from every
opposite-sign atom in the same, preceding, and succeeding blocks.
Choose \(\kappa\) so that
\(C_{\alpha,d,r}\kappa^\beta<a_r\).  Data processing to
\(\{E_j,E_j^c\}\), followed by
Lemma~\ref{lem:bernoulli-kl-linear-separation}, gives
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|
            p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)\ge c w_j.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 s_j^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|
                    p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 \ge cR_j^{2r}w_j^{1+2r/\beta}
 =ca_j^qR_j^{2r-\rho q}.
\]
The final exponent is positive exactly when \(\rho<p=2r/q\).
Recursive enlargement of \(R_j\) proves
\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-sharpness}.  Finally, for \(\rho<r\), a
one-dimensional Pareto law supported on the \(e\)-axis may have finite
\(\rho\)th and infinite \(r\)th absolute moment, proving the stated domain
obstruction.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Stable Gaussian-quadrature entropy threshold]
\label{cor:stable-gaussian-quadrature-threshold}
Let \(0<\alpha<2\), \(n\ge1\), and let \(\nu\) be a probability law on
\(\RR\) such that
\[
 \EE|X|^{2n-1}<\infty,\qquad |\operatorname{supp}\nu|\ge n.
\]
Let \(G_n\nu\) and \(\pi_n\) be its \(n\)-node Gaussian quadrature law and
monic degree-\(n\) orthogonal polynomial, respectively.  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-gaussian-quadrature-finite}
 \EE|X|^{2n}<\infty
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \lim_{s\to\infty}s^{4n}
 D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,1)}*\nu\|
            p_s^{(\alpha,1)}*G_n\nu)
 =C_{\alpha,n}\|\pi_n\|_{L^2(\nu)}^4,
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-gaussian-quadrature-constant}
 C_{\alpha,n}:=
 \frac1{2((2n)!)^2}\int_{\RR}
 \frac{(\partial^{2n}p_1^{(\alpha,1)}(y))^2}
      {p_1^{(\alpha,1)}(y)}\dd y>0.
\end{equation}
On the other hand,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-gaussian-quadrature-infinite}
 \EE|X|^{2n}=\infty
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 s^{4n}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,1)}*\nu\|
                  p_s^{(\alpha,1)}*G_n\nu)\longrightarrow+\infty.
\end{equation}
Consequently, finiteness of the \(2n\)th absolute moment is equivalent to
boundedness of the scaled relative entropy in
\eqref{eq:stable-gaussian-quadrature-finite}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Since \(1+\alpha<2(2n)\), the all-order critical exponent at \(r=2n\) is
\(p_{2n,\alpha,1}=2n\).  Gaussian exactness through degree \(2n-1\) and
\eqref{eq:gauss-missing-moment-norm} show that the first unmatched moment is
\(\|\pi_n\|_{L^2(\nu)}^2\).  Theorem
\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} therefore gives
\eqref{eq:stable-gaussian-quadrature-finite} and
\eqref{eq:stable-gaussian-quadrature-constant}.  If this moment difference
vanishes, \(\nu=G_n\nu\), and the same formula holds with both sides zero.
Strict positivity of \(C_{\alpha,n}\) also follows from the Fourier argument
in that theorem.

For the converse, define
\[
 R_n(u):=(-1)^n\left\{\cos u-
       \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{(-1)^ku^{2k}}{(2k)!}\right\}.
\]
One has \(R_1=1-\cos\ge0\), while
\(R_n''=R_{n-1}\) and \(R_n(0)=R_n'(0)=0\).  Induction therefore gives
\(R_n\ge0\) on \(\RR\).  Moreover,
\(s^{2n}R_n(x/s)\to x^{2n}/(2n)!\).  If the \(2n\)th moment of \(\nu\) is
infinite, Fatou's lemma gives
\[
 s^{2n}\int R_n(x/s)\nu(\dd x)\longrightarrow+\infty.
\]
The corresponding integral for the finite-support law \(G_n\nu\) remains
bounded.  Since all even moments below \(2n\) agree, it follows that
\[
 s^{2n}\left|\Re\{\varphi_\nu(1/s)
                 -\varphi_{G_n\nu}(1/s)\}\right|\longrightarrow+\infty.
\]
At frequency \(1/s\), stable smoothing multiplies this difference by the
fixed nonzero number \(\widehat p_1^{(\alpha,1)}(1)\).  The dual
characterization of total variation and Pinsker's inequality now imply
\eqref{eq:stable-gaussian-quadrature-infinite}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The law-by-law finite-covariance decomposition}

The preceding theorem optimizes over moment classes.  The next theorem gives
the exact law-by-law interface under finite covariance alone.  It separates
the universal quadratic covariance energy from the full nonlinear energy of
the raw tail beyond the smoothing scale.

\begin{theorem}[Stable law-by-law tail decomposition]
\label{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition}
Let \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<2\), and let \(\nu\) be a centred probability law
on \(\RR^d\) with finite covariance matrix \(\Sigma\).  Put
\[
 H_{\alpha,d}(s):=
 D_{\rm KL}\!\left(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\,\middle\|\,
 p_s^{(\alpha,d)}\right)
\]

 succeeded in 176ms:
\]
Thus bounded scaled entropy forces finite covariance.  Given \(0<r<2\),
choose \(a\in(\max\{1,r\},2)\) and put symmetric masses proportional to
\(n^{-a-1}\) at \(\pm ne_1\), with the remaining mass at zero.  This law
has mean zero and finite \(r\)th moment but infinite variance, so its scaled
entropy has infinite limsup.

It remains to prove optimality between two and \(p\) when \(\beta>4\).
Fix \(2\le r<p\), choose positive \(a_j\) with \(\sum_ja_j<\infty\), and
put symmetric masses \(w_j/2\) at \(\pm R_je_1\), where
\(w_j=a_jR_j^{-r}\).  Add a sufficiently small bounded symmetric spanning
component.  The resulting law has positive-definite finite covariance and
finite \(r\)th moment.  Set
\[
 s_j=\kappa R_jw_j^{1/\beta},\qquad
 A_j=B(R_je_1,s_j).
\]
The component at \(R_je_1\) gives
\((p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu)(A_j)\ge c_{\alpha,d}w_j\).  On the other hand,
\eqref{eq:stable-input-density} and \(s_j/R_j\to0\) give
\[
 p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}(A_j)
 \le C_{\alpha,d}(s_j/R_j)^\beta
 =C_{\alpha,d}\kappa^\beta w_j.
\]
Choose \(\kappa\) so that
\(C_{\alpha,d}\kappa^\beta<c_{\alpha,d}\).  Data processing to
\(\{A_j,A_j^c\}\) and
Lemma~\ref{lem:bernoulli-kl-linear-separation} then yield
\(H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)\ge c w_j\), and hence
\[
 s_j^4H_{\alpha,d}(s_j)
 \ge cR_j^4w_j^{1+4/\beta}
 =ca_j^{q_{\alpha,d}}R_j^{4-rq_{\alpha,d}}.
\]
Here \(q_{\alpha,d}=1+4/\beta\) and
\(r<p=4/q_{\alpha,d}\), so the exponent of \(R_j\) is positive.
Recursive choice of the radii makes \(s_j\to\infty\) and the last display
unbounded while preserving all moment assertions.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[All-order stable critical remainder]
\label{lem:all-order-stable-critical-remainder}
Let \(r\ge1\), put \(\beta=d+\alpha\), and define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:all-order-stable-critical-exponents}
 q_{r,\alpha,d}:=\min\left\{2,1+\frac{2r}{d+\alpha}\right\},
 \qquad
 p_{r,\alpha,d}:=\frac{2r}{q_{r,\alpha,d}}
 =\max\left\{r,\frac{2r(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+2r}\right\}.
\end{equation}
Let \(q=q_{r,\alpha,d}\), \(p=p_{r,\alpha,d}\), and
\(m=\lfloor p\rfloor\).  If \(T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(y,z)\) is the Taylor
polynomial of \(F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\) at zero through degree \(m\), then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder}
 \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
 \le C_{\alpha,d,r}
 \begin{cases}
  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\le1,\\
  |z|^p,&|z|>1,
 \end{cases}
 \le C_{\alpha,d,r}|z|^p.
\end{equation}
Consequently, if a probability law \(\lambda\) on \(\RR^d\) has finite
\(p\)th absolute moment and
\[
 q_s^\lambda(y):=\int F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),
\]
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:all-order-stable-integrated-remainder}
 q_s^\lambda
 =1+\sum_{j=1}^m s^{-j}B_j^\lambda+r_s^\lambda,
 \qquad
 \|r_s^\lambda\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-p}),
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}\label{eq:all-order-stable-moment-modes}
 B_j^\lambda(y):=
 \frac{(-1)^j}{p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)}
 \sum_{|\gamma|=j}\frac{m_\gamma(\lambda)}{\gamma!}
 \partial^\gamma p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y),
 \qquad
 m_\gamma(\lambda):=\int x^\gamma\lambda(\dd x).
\end{equation}
Every \(B_j^\lambda\) in this display is bounded.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The proof of \eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} applies verbatim for
every fixed \(1<q\le2\) and gives
\[
 \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)\|_{L^q(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}
 \le C(1+|z|)^{\beta(1-1/q)}.
\]
The local Taylor argument in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder} gives the first line
of \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder}.  For \(|z|>1\), the
Taylor modes are bounded by
Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}, and
hence
\[
 \|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,z)\|_q
 \le C\{|z|^{\beta(1-1/q)}+|z|^m\}\le C|z|^p.
\]
Indeed, \(m\le p\), while
\(\beta(1-1/q)\le p\); in the non-Hilbert regime
\(\beta>2r\), both sides of the latter inequality equal
\(2r\beta/(\beta+2r)\).  Since \(m+1>p\), the final inequality in
\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder} also holds on the unit ball.

Taylor's formula gives \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-integrated-remainder}
before its norm assertion.  For fixed \(x\), the local estimate implies
\[
 s^p\|F_\cdot^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)
       -T_m^{(\alpha,d)}(\cdot,x/s)\|_q\longrightarrow0,
\]
whereas \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder} bounds this expression
by \(C|x|^p\).  Minkowski's inequality and dominated convergence prove the
claimed \(L^q\) remainder.  Boundedness of the modes follows again from
Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Two-background critical Bregman transfer]
\label{lem:two-background-critical-bregman-transfer}
Let \(1<q\le2\), \(p\ge r>0\), and \(pq=2r\).  On a probability space
\((E,\Omega)\), suppose \(g_s\ge c_s>0\),
\[
 \int g_s\dd\Omega=1,\qquad c_s\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad \|g_s-1\|_{L^1(\Omega)}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Let \(B\in L^\infty(\Omega)\), and suppose
\[
 v_s=s^{-r}B+o(s^{-r})\quad\hbox{in }L^\infty(\Omega),
 \qquad \|e_s\|_{L^q(\Omega)}=o(s^{-p}).
\]
If \(g_s+v_s+e_s\ge0\) and both \(g_s\Omega\) and
\((g_s+v_s+e_s)\Omega\) are probability measures, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-background-critical-bregman-transfer}
 D_{\rm KL}((g_s+v_s+e_s)\Omega\|g_s\Omega)
 =\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int B^2\dd\Omega+o(s^{-2r}).
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

The hypotheses on the denominator in this lemma deliberately stop short of
\(L^\infty\)-convergence to one.  They require only a positive lower bound
approaching one, mass normalization, and \(L^1\)-convergence.  This weaker
interface is what permits a heavy-tailed translated mixture to serve as the
background.

\begin{proof}
For \(g>0\), write \(\Psi_g(z)=g\Phi(z/g)\).  Scaling
Lemma~\ref{lem:critical-lq-kl-perturbation} shows, whenever
\(|v/g|\le1/4\) and \(g+v+e\ge0\), that
\[
 0\le\Psi_g(v+e)-\Psi_g(v)
      -\log(1+v/g)e\le C_q g^{1-q}|e|^q.
\]
For large \(s\), the hypotheses give \(g_s\ge1/2\) and
\(\|v_s/g_s\|_\infty\le1/4\).  Therefore H\"older's inequality yields
\begin{align*}
 &\left|D_{\rm KL}((g_s+v_s+e_s)\Omega\|g_s\Omega)
       -\int\Psi_{g_s}(v_s)\dd\Omega\right|\\
 &\qquad\le
 C\|v_s\|_{L^{q/(q-1)}}\|e_s\|_{L^q}
 +C\|e_s\|_{L^q}^q
 =o(s^{-r-p})+o(s^{-pq})=o(s^{-2r}).
\end{align*}
Uniform Taylor expansion at zero gives
\[
 \int\Psi_{g_s}(v_s)\dd\Omega
 =\frac12\int\frac{v_s^2}{g_s}\dd\Omega+O(\|v_s\|_\infty^3).
\]
Finally,
\[
 \left|\int B^2(g_s^{-1}-1)\dd\Omega\right|
 \le2\|B\|_\infty^2\|g_s-1\|_1\longrightarrow0,
\]
and \eqref{eq:two-background-critical-bregman-transfer} follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite-difference moment blocks]
\label{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}
Let \(r\ge1\), let \(e\) be a unit vector, and define
\[
 \sigma_R:=2^{1-r}\sum_{k=0}^r(-1)^{r-k}\binom rk
                 \delta_{(k+1)Re}=A_R^+-A_R^-.
\]
Then \(A_R^+\) and \(A_R^-\) are probability measures and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-block-moment-identities}
 \int x^\gamma\dd\sigma_R(x)=0\quad(|\gamma|<r),
 \qquad
 \int(e\cdot x)^r\dd\sigma_R(x)=2^{1-r}r!R^r.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The positive and negative binomial coefficients each sum to \(2^{r-1}\),
and the order-\(r\) forward-difference identity gives
\eqref{eq:stable-block-moment-identities}.  In particular, when \(r=1\),
\(\sigma_R=\delta_{2Re}-\delta_{Re}\); the same cancellation and nonzero
first-difference conclusions hold without a separate construction.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Moving-ball probability separation]
\label{lem:stable-moving-ball-probability-separation}
Let \(\beta=d+\alpha\), let \(A_R^\pm\) be the blocks in
Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}, and suppose
\[
 R_{j+1}>4(r+1)R_j,
 \qquad w_j>0,
 \qquad \sum_jw_j<1.
\]
Define
\[
 \nu=\left(1-\sum_jw_j\right)\delta_0+\sum_jw_jA_{R_j}^+,
 \qquad
 \eta=\left(1-\sum_jw_j\right)\delta_0+\sum_jw_jA_{R_j}^-.
\]
Put \(x_j=(r+1)R_je\), choose
\(s_j=\kappa R_jw_j^{1/\beta}<R_j/4\), and set
\(E_j=B(x_j,s_j)\).  There are constants \(a_r>0\) and
\(C_{\alpha,d,r}<\infty\), independent of \(j,\kappa,R_j,w_j\), such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-moving-ball-probability-separation}
 (p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu)(E_j)\ge a_rw_j,
 \qquad
 (p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)(E_j)
 \le C_{\alpha,d,r}\kappa^\beta w_j.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The endpoint coefficient in \(A_{R_j}^+\) at \(x_j\) is \(2^{1-r}\).
Stable scaling and positivity therefore give
\[
 (p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu)(E_j)
 \ge 2^{1-r}w_j\int_{B(0,1)}p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(y)\dd y
 =:a_rw_j.
\]
We verify the separation from every atom of \(\eta\).  In block \(j\),
opposite-sign atoms are at least \(R_j\) from \(x_j\).  Every earlier atom
has norm at most \((r+1)R_{j-1}<R_j/4\), whereas every later atom has norm at
least \(R_{j+1}>4(r+1)R_j\); the atom at zero obeys the earlier-atom bound.
After subtracting the radius \(s_j<R_j/4\), every such atom \(z\) satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stable-moving-ball-distance}
 \operatorname{dist}(z,E_j)\ge3R_j/4.
\end{equation}
For \(y\in E_j\), the stable density upper bound and scaling now give
\[
 p_{s_j}^{(\alpha,d)}(y-z)
 \le C_{\alpha,d,r}s_j^\alpha R_j^{-\beta}.
\]

"""Numerical checks for the Cayley--Poisson moment-equivalence hierarchy.

The computation is deterministic.  It evaluates

    H(t) = int Phi(E[R_{X/t}] - 1) d omega,

in the Cayley angle, computes the universal coefficients by Laurent
constant-term extraction, and compares the scaled residuals.  Symmetric
Pareto laws have P(|X| > x) = x**(-alpha), x >= 1, so their q-th absolute
moment is finite exactly for q < alpha.  The boundary alpha = 2m-2 is the
regularly-varying test with the claimed top moment infinite.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import itertools
import json
import math
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

import numpy as np
from scipy.special import roots_laguerre


def _compositions(total: int, parts: int, minimum: int = 2) -> Iterable[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    if parts == 1:
        if total >= minimum:
            yield (total,)
        return
    for first in range(minimum, total - minimum * (parts - 1) + 1):
        for rest in _compositions(total - first, parts - 1, minimum):
            yield (first,) + rest


def laurent_mode(n: int) -> Dict[int, complex]:
    """Return Q_n from the manuscript's fixed Laurent convention."""
    scale = ((-1j) ** n) / (2**n)
    out: Dict[int, complex] = {}
    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        coefficient = scale * math.comb(n - 1, k - 1)
        out[k] = coefficient
        out[-k] = coefficient * ((-1) ** n)
    return out


def mode_integral(indices: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Compute J(indices) as the constant term of the Laurent product."""
    product: Dict[int, complex] = {0: 1.0}
    for n in indices:
        next_product: Dict[int, complex] = {}
        for a, ca in product.items():
            for b, cb in laurent_mode(n).items():
                next_product[a + b] = next_product.get(a + b, 0.0) + ca * cb
        product = next_product
    value = product.get(0, 0.0)
    if abs(value.imag) > 2e-12:
        raise ArithmeticError(f"non-real mode integral J{tuple(indices)}={value}")
    return float(value.real)


def entropy_coefficient(m: int, moments: Dict[int, float]) -> float:
    """Evaluate A_{2m} from the universal coefficient formula."""
    if m < 2:
        raise ValueError("m must be at least 2")
    total = 2 * m
    answer = 0.0
    for r in range(2, m + 1):
        prefactor = ((-1) ** r) / (r * (r - 1))
        for indices in _compositions(total, r):
            moment_product = 1.0
            for n in indices:
                value = moments.get(n)
                if value is None or not math.isfinite(value):
                    raise ValueError(f"moment {n} is not finite")
                moment_product *= value
            answer += prefactor * moment_product * mode_integral(indices)
    return answer


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SymmetricPareto:
    alpha: float
    name: str

    def moment(self, order: int) -> float:
        if order % 2:
            return 0.0
        if order >= self.alpha:
            return math.inf
        return self.alpha / (self.alpha - order)

    def quadrature(self, count: int) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        # If Z is Exp(1), then |X|=exp(Z/alpha) has the required Pareto tail.
        nodes, weights = roots_laguerre(count)
        nodes = np.asarray(nodes, dtype=np.longdouble)
        # Windows aliases longdouble to float64.  Nodes beyond this threshold
        # have exponentially negligible Laguerre weight but squaring their
        # Pareto magnitudes would overflow float64.
        keep = nodes / np.longdouble(self.alpha) < 300
        nodes = nodes[keep]
        weights = weights[keep]
        magnitudes = np.exp(nodes / np.longdouble(self.alpha))
        weights = np.asarray(weights, dtype=np.longdouble)
        weights = weights / np.sum(weights)
        return magnitudes, weights


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SymmetricAtomic:
    magnitudes: Tuple[float, ...]
    probabilities: Tuple[float, ...]
    name: str

    def moment(self, order: int) -> float:
        if order % 2:
            return 0.0
        return sum(p * (x**order) for x, p in zip(self.magnitudes, self.probabilities))

    def quadrature(self, count: int) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        del count
        return np.asarray(self.magnitudes), np.asarray(self.probabilities)


def _phi(s: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Stable evaluation of (1+s) log(1+s)-s near zero."""
    out = np.empty_like(s, dtype=np.longdouble)
    small = np.abs(s) < np.longdouble("0.02")
    if np.any(small):
        z = s[small]
        term = z * z
        series = term / 2
        for r in range(3, 18):
            term *= z
            series += ((-1) ** r) * term / (r * (r - 1))
        out[small] = series
    if np.any(~small):
        z = s[~small]
        out[~small] = (1 + z) * np.log1p(z) - z
    return out


class EntropyQuadrature:
    def __init__(self, angle_count: int = 480, tail_count: int = 180):
        nodes, weights = np.polynomial.legendre.leggauss(angle_count)
        self.theta = np.asarray((math.pi / 2) * nodes, dtype=np.longdouble)
        # omega(dy)=d theta/pi, so mapped Legendre weights are weights/2.
        self.angle_weights = np.asarray(weights / 2, dtype=np.longdouble)
        self.tail_count = tail_count

    def h(self, law, t: float) -> float:
        magnitudes, probabilities = law.quadrature(self.tail_count)
        a = np.asarray(magnitudes, dtype=np.longdouble) / np.longdouble(t)
        p = np.asarray(probabilities, dtype=np.longdouble)
        p /= np.sum(p)
        c = np.cos(self.theta)
        s = np.sin(self.theta)
        cs = c * s
        c2 = c * c
        delta = np.zeros_like(self.theta)
        # Chunking bounds memory for the full (tail node) x (angle node) array.
        for start in range(0, len(a), 48):
            aa = a[start : start + 48, None]
            pp = p[start : start + 48, None]
            quadratic = aa * aa * c2[None, :]
            linear = 2 * aa * cs[None, :]
            pair = np.longdouble("0.5") * (
                1 / (1 - linear + quadratic) + 1 / (1 + linear + quadratic)
            )
            delta += np.sum(pp * (pair - 1), axis=0)
        if np.min(1 + delta) <= 0:
            raise ArithmeticError("quadrature produced a nonpositive density quotient")
        return float(np.sum(self.angle_weights * _phi(delta)))


def finite_moments(law, top: int) -> Dict[int, float]:
    return {n: law.moment(n) for n in range(2, top + 1)}


def scaled_residual(law, m: int, t: float, quadrature: EntropyQuadrature) -> float:
    h_value = quadrature.h(law, t)
    lower = 0.0
    for j in range(2, m):
        lower += entropy_coefficient(j, finite_moments(law, 2 * j - 2)) * t ** (-2 * j)
    return (t ** (2 * m)) * (h_value - lower)


def _finite_check(law, m: int, times: Sequence[float], quadrature: EntropyQuadrature) -> dict:
    exact = entropy_coefficient(m, finite_moments(law, 2 * m - 2))
    scaled = [scaled_residual(law, m, t, quadrature) for t in times]
    scale = max(1.0, abs(exact))
    errors = [abs(x - exact) / scale for x in scaled]
    # Heavy tails can converge slowly.  The check requires visible movement
    # toward the exact Laurent coefficient and a moderate final discrepancy.
    passed = errors[-1] < 0.35 and min(errors[-2:]) <= min(errors[:2])
    return {
        "law": law.name,
        "m": m,
        "moment_order": 2 * m - 2,
        "moment_finite": True,
        "times": list(times),
        "scaled_residual": scaled,
        "exact_A": exact,
        "relative_errors": errors,
        "passed": passed,
    }


def _boundary_check(law, m: int, times: Sequence[float], quadrature: EntropyQuadrature) -> dict:
    scaled = [scaled_residual(law, m, t, quadrature) for t in times]
    kappa = ((-1) ** m) * (m - 1) * (2 ** (-2 * m + 2))
    if m == 2:
        sign_ok = scaled[-1] > 0
    else:
        sign_ok = math.copysign(1.0, scaled[-1]) == math.copysign(1.0, kappa)
    growth = abs(scaled[-1]) > 1.12 * abs(scaled[0])
    return {
        "law": law.name,
        "m": m,
        "moment_order": 2 * m - 2,
        "moment_finite": False,
        "times": list(times),
        "scaled_residual": scaled,
        "expected_boundary_behavior": "(log t)^2" if m == 2 else "signed log t",
        "expected_sign": 1 if m == 2 else int(math.copysign(1, kappa)),
        "passed": bool(sign_ok and growth),
    }


def run_battery(quick: bool = False) -> dict:
    max_m = 4 if quick else 5
    times = (5.0, 7.0, 10.0, 14.0) if quick else (5.0, 7.0, 10.0, 14.0, 20.0)
    quadrature = EntropyQuadrature(
        angle_count=320 if quick else 560,
        tail_count=120 if quick else 210,
    )
    checks: List[dict] = []
    failed_checks: List[str] = []

    for m in range(2, max_m + 1):
        p = 2 * m - 2
        finite_law = SymmetricPareto(alpha=p + 6.0, name=f"Pareto(alpha={p + 6:g})")
        boundary_law = SymmetricPareto(alpha=float(p), name=f"Pareto-boundary(alpha={p:g})")
        for check in (
            _finite_check(finite_law, m, times, quadrature),
            _boundary_check(boundary_law, m, times, quadrature),
        ):
            checks.append(check)
            if not check["passed"]:
                failed_checks.append(f"{check['law']}, m={m}")

    # Explicit converse search: all candidates have the claimed top moment.
    # A candidate is recorded only when its large-t scaled residual fails both
    # to approach the exact A and the deterministic quadrature sanity checks.
    counterexamples: List[dict] = []
    search_rows: List[dict] = []
    atomic = SymmetricAtomic((1.0, 2.0), (0.7, 0.3), "two-radius compact law")
    for m in range(2, max_m + 1):
        p = 2 * m - 2
        candidates = [
            SymmetricPareto(p + 2.0, f"search Pareto(alpha={p + 2:g})"),
            SymmetricPareto(p + 6.0, f"search Pareto(alpha={p + 6:g})"),
            atomic,
        ]
        for law in candidates:
            row = _finite_check(law, m, times, quadrature)
            search_rows.append(row)
            if not row["passed"]:
                counterexamples.append(row)

    return {
        "description": "Cayley--Poisson sharp moment-equivalence numerical battery",
        "orders_checked": max_m - 1,
        "m_range": [2, max_m],
        "checks": checks,
        "failed_checks": failed_checks,
        "counterexample_search": search_rows,
        "counterexamples": counterexamples,
        "quadrature": {
            "angle_nodes": len(quadrature.theta),
            "pareto_laguerre_nodes": quadrature.tail_count,
        },
    }


def _format_report(report: dict) -> str:
    lines = [
        report["description"],
        f"orders m={report['m_range'][0]}..{report['m_range'][1]}",
        f"quadrature={report['quadrature']}",
        "",
        "FINITE/BOUNDARY BATTERY",
    ]
    for row in report["checks"]:
        lines.append(
            f"m={row['m']} p={row['moment_order']} law={row['law']} "
            f"moment_finite={row['moment_finite']} passed={row['passed']}"
        )
        lines.append("  t=" + ", ".join(f"{x:g}" for x in row["times"]))
        lines.append(
            "  t^(2m) residual=" + ", ".join(f"{x:.10g}" for x in row["scaled_residual"])
        )
        if row["moment_finite"]:
            lines.append(f"  exact A_(2m)={row['exact_A']:.10g}")
        else:
            lines.append(
                f"  expected={row['expected_boundary_behavior']}, sign={row['expected_sign']}"
            )
    lines.extend(["", "EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE SEARCH"])
    for row in report["counterexample_search"]:
        lines.append(
            f"m={row['m']} law={row['law']} exact={row['exact_A']:.8g} "
            f"last_scaled={row['scaled_residual'][-1]:.8g} passed={row['passed']}"
        )
    lines.extend(
        [
            "",
            f"failed battery checks: {len(report['failed_checks'])}",
            f"counterexamples found: {len(report['counterexamples'])}",
            "RESULT: PASS" if not report["failed_checks"] and not report["counterexamples"] else "RESULT: FAIL",
        ]
    )
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv=()) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--quick", action="store_true", help="smaller deterministic test battery")
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="emit JSON instead of the text report")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, help="write the report with LF line endings")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    report = run_battery(quick=args.quick)
    formatted = json.dumps(report, indent=2) if args.json else _format_report(report)
    if args.output is None:
        print(formatted, end="")
    else:
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.output.write_text(formatted, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        print(formatted, end="")
    return 0 if not report["failed_checks"] and not report["counterexamples"] else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""Verification battery for the regular-variation entropy boundary theorem.

The checks are deterministic:

1. exact Laurent constant terms are compared with the theorem's kappa_N;
2. logarithmic-Pareto models test the Karamata truncated-moment scale;
3. the unconditional quotient jet is tested in L-infinity on a Cayley grid;
4. full KL quadrature tests the sign, scale, and convergence direction;
5. a parameter scan searches for counterexamples to the necessary
   divergent-integral hypothesis.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import math
import sys
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from dataclasses import dataclass
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import quad
from scipy.special import roots_laguerre

from verify_moment_equivalence import (
    EntropyQuadrature,
    entropy_coefficient,
    finite_moments,
    mode_integral,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LogParetoBoundary:
    """Symmetric law with density proportional to y^(-p-1)(log y)^(-a).

    A mass tail_mass is split equally between +/-Y, Y >= e, and the
    remaining mass is at zero. Its absolute tail is asymptotic to

        C y^(-p) (log y)^(-a),   C = tail_mass / (p * Z),

    where Z normalizes the positive-magnitude density.
    """

    p: int
    a: float
    tail_mass: float = 0.05

    @property
    def z_normalizer(self) -> float:
        value, _ = quad(
            lambda z: math.exp(-self.p * z) * z ** (-self.a),
            1.0,
            np.inf,
            epsabs=2e-14,
            epsrel=2e-13,
        )
        return value

    @property
    def tail_constant(self) -> float:
        return self.tail_mass / (self.p * self.z_normalizer)

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return f"log-Pareto(p={self.p}, a={self.a:g})"

    def ell(self, t: float) -> float:
        if t <= math.e:
            return 0.0
        upper = math.log(t)
        if self.a == 1.0:
            return math.log(upper)
        return (upper ** (1.0 - self.a) - 1.0) / (1.0 - self.a)

    def truncated_boundary_moment(self, t: float) -> float:
        return self.tail_mass * self.ell(t) / self.z_normalizer

    def boundary_moment_finite(self) -> bool:
        return self.a > 1.0

    def boundary_moment(self) -> float:
        if not self.boundary_moment_finite():
            return math.inf
        return self.tail_mass / (self.z_normalizer * (self.a - 1.0))

    def moment(self, order: int) -> float:
        if order % 2:
            return 0.0
        if order == 0:
            return 1.0
        if order == self.p:
            return self.boundary_moment()
        if order > self.p:
            return math.inf
        rate = self.p - order
        value, _ = quad(
            lambda z: math.exp(-rate * z) * z ** (-self.a),
            1.0,
            np.inf,
            epsabs=2e-13,
            epsrel=2e-12,
        )
        return self.tail_mass * value / self.z_normalizer

    def quadrature(self, count: int) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        nodes, weights = roots_laguerre(count)
        z = 1.0 + nodes / self.p
        tilting = z ** (-self.a)
        probabilities = weights * tilting
        probabilities /= np.sum(probabilities)
        magnitudes = np.exp(z)
        magnitudes = np.concatenate(([0.0], magnitudes))
        probabilities = np.concatenate(
            ([1.0 - self.tail_mass], self.tail_mass * probabilities)
        )
        return magnitudes, probabilities


def quotient(law: LogParetoBoundary, t: float, y: np.ndarray, count: int) -> np.ndarray:
    magnitudes, probabilities = law.quadrature(count)
    a = magnitudes[:, None] / t
    yy = y[None, :]
    pair = 0.5 * (
        (1.0 + yy * yy) / (1.0 + (yy - a) ** 2)
        + (1.0 + yy * yy) / (1.0 + (yy + a) ** 2)
    )
    return np.sum(probabilities[:, None] * pair, axis=0) - 1.0


def u_mode(n: int, y: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    # Stable three-term recurrence from the generating denominator.
    if n == 0:
        return np.ones_like(y)
    denominator = 1.0 + y * y
    u0 = np.ones_like(y)
    u1 = 2.0 * y / denominator
    if n == 1:
        return u1
    for _ in range(2, n + 1):
        u0, u1 = u1, (2.0 * y * u1 - u0) / denominator
    return u1


def verify_constants() -> List[Dict[str, object]]:
    rows = []
    for n_order in range(3, 8):
        p = 2 * n_order - 2
        exact = mode_integral((2, p))
        formula = ((-1) ** n_order) * (n_order - 1) * 2 ** (-2 * n_order + 2)
        rows.append(
            {
                "N": n_order,
                "p": p,
                "constant_term": exact,
                "formula": formula,
                "passed": abs(exact - formula) < 2e-14,
            }
        )
    return rows


def verify_moments() -> List[Dict[str, object]]:
    rows: List[Dict[str, object]] = []
    times = (1e2, 1e4, 1e8, 1e16)
    for a in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0):
        law = LogParetoBoundary(4, a)
        ratios = [
            law.truncated_boundary_moment(t)
            / (law.p * law.tail_constant * law.ell(t))
            for t in times
        ]
        rows.append(
            {
                "law": law.name,
                "times": times,
                "M_over_pC_ell": ratios,
                "passed": max(abs(value - 1.0) for value in ratios) < 5e-12,
            }
        )
    return rows


def verify_quotient_jets() -> List[Dict[str, object]]:
    theta = np.linspace(-1.54, 1.54, 601)
    y = np.tan(theta)
    rows: List[Dict[str, object]] = []
    for a in (0.0, 1.0):
        law = LogParetoBoundary(4, a)
        ratios = []
        for t in (20.0, 50.0, 120.0, 300.0):
            delta = quotient(law, t, y, count=220)
            finite = np.zeros_like(y)
            for n in range(2, law.p):
                finite += law.moment(n) * u_mode(n, y) * t ** (-n)
            top = (
                u_mode(law.p, y)
                * t ** (-law.p)
                * law.truncated_boundary_moment(t)
            )
            error = float(np.max(np.abs(delta - finite - top)))
            scale = t ** (-law.p) * law.truncated_boundary_moment(t)
            ratios.append(error / scale)
        # The asymptotic is slow, especially at a=1; require net decay.
        passed = ratios[-1] < ratios[0] and ratios[-1] < 0.8
        rows.append(
            {
                "law": law.name,
                "times": (20.0, 50.0, 120.0, 300.0),
                "sup_error_over_boundary_mode": ratios,
                "passed": passed,
            }
        )
    return rows


def verify_full_entropy() -> List[Dict[str, object]]:
    quadrature = EntropyQuadrature(angle_count=720, tail_count=240)
    rows: List[Dict[str, object]] = []
    for a in (0.0, 1.0):
        law = LogParetoBoundary(4, a)
        mu2 = law.moment(2)
        a4 = entropy_coefficient(2, finite_moments(law, 2))
        kappa = -1.0 / 8.0
        normalized = []
        # Both models are beyond their small-t transient on this interval.
        # The log-log model has a shallow pre-asymptotic maximum near t=28.
        times = (28.0, 40.0, 60.0, 90.0, 140.0)
        for t in times:
            h = quadrature.h(law, t)
            residual = t**6 * (h - a4 * t ** (-4))
            normalized.append(residual / (kappa * mu2 * law.truncated_boundary_moment(t)))
        # Full entropy convergence contains an O(1)/M term and is deliberately
        # tested only for correct sign and movement toward the limit one.
        errors = [abs(value - 1.0) for value in normalized]
        passed = normalized[-1] > 0.0 and errors[-1] < errors[0]
        rows.append(
            {
                "law": law.name,
                "times": times,
                "residual_over_kappa_mu2_M": normalized,
                "passed": passed,
            }
        )
    return rows


def counterexample_search() -> Dict[str, object]:
    rows = []
    false_classifications = []
    for a in np.linspace(-0.5, 2.0, 26):
        law = LogParetoBoundary(4, float(a))
        integral_diverges = a <= 1.0
        moment_finite = law.boundary_moment_finite()
        classification_ok = moment_finite == (not integral_diverges)
        row = {
            "a": float(a),
            "integrated_factor_diverges": integral_diverges,
            "p_moment_finite": moment_finite,
            "classification_ok": classification_ok,
        }
        rows.append(row)
        if not classification_ok:
            false_classifications.append(row)
    return {
        "candidates": len(rows),
        "false_classifications": false_classifications,
        "finite-boundary-example": {
            "a": 1.5,
            "meaning": (
                "tail index remains p, but integral L(s) ds/s converges and "
                "the p-th moment is finite"
            ),
        },
        "passed": not false_classifications,
    }


def _run_verification() -> int:
    sections = {
        "laurent_constants": verify_constants(),
        "tauberian_moments": verify_moments(),
        "quotient_jets": verify_quotient_jets(),
        "full_entropy": verify_full_entropy(),
        "counterexample_search": counterexample_search(),
    }
    failures = []
    for name, section in sections.items():
        if isinstance(section, list):
            failures.extend(
                f"{name}:{row.get('law', row.get('N'))}"
                for row in section
                if not row["passed"]
            )
        elif not section["passed"]:
            failures.append(name)

    print("REGULAR-VARIATION BOUNDARY-LAYER VERIFICATION")
    for name, section in sections.items():
        print(f"\n[{name}]")
        if isinstance(section, list):
            for row in section:
                print(row)
        else:
            print(section)
    print(f"\nfailures={failures}")
    print("RESULT: PASS" if not failures else "RESULT: FAIL")
    return 0 if not failures else 1


def main(argv=()) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.output is None:
        return _run_verification()

    capture = StringIO()
    with redirect_stdout(capture):
        status = _run_verification()
    report = capture.getvalue()
    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.output.write_text(report, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(report, end="")
    return status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
INPUT_RE = re.compile(r"\\input\{([^}]+)\}")


def read_tex_source(path: Path) -> str:
    """Read a TeX source together with any local input wrappers."""

    source = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def expand(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        child = ROOT / match.group(1)
        if child.suffix == "":
            child = child.with_suffix(".tex")
        return read_tex_source(child)

    return INPUT_RE.sub(expand, source)
