+\section{Fixed-scale proxy conventions}\label{app:stable-proxy-conventions}
+
+We record the convention invariance used after
+Corollary~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Let
+\(\theta:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]\) be measurable, with \(\theta=0\) on
+\([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\) on \([2,\infty)\), and fix \(c>0\).  For
+\(\lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\}\), put
+\[
+ \chi_s(x)=\theta(|x|/(cs)),\qquad
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\int\chi_s(x)\lambda(\dd x),
+\]
+\[
+ V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+ =\int\chi_s(x)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+The hard convention is obtained by taking
+\(\theta=\mathbf1_{(1,\infty)}\).  With the common lower-order jet
+\(C_{r-1,s}\) from that corollary, define
+\[
+ A_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ =1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-	au_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \widetilde A_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ =\frac{1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+        {1+\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}.
+\]
+
+\begin{proposition}[Robustness of the fixed-scale tail-jet convention]
+\label{prop:stable-proxy-convention-robustness}
+Under the hypotheses of
+Corollary~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, both
+pairs above are positive probability densities relative to
+\(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\) for all sufficiently large \(s\), and their relative
+entropies are finite.  For either the hard or a smooth fixed-scale retention
+and either additive or multiplicative normalization, write the resulting
+proxy entropy as \(\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\rm conv}\).  Then
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\rm conv}
+  +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Consequently, any two of these fixed-scale conventions have proxy entropies
+that differ by \(o(s^{-2r})\), and the condition
+\(s^{2r}\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\rm conv}\to0\) is independent of the stated
+retention and normalization choices.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), and let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) denote the
+homogeneous order-\(j\) Taylor term used in the proof of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-positive-tail-jet-kernel}.  Direct addition and
+subtraction of the Taylor terms gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:convention-exact-tail-split}
+ q_s^\lambda=A_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}B_r^\lambda
+                  +R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
+\end{equation}
+where
+\begin{align*}
+ R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
+ &=\int(1-\chi_s(x))
+   \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
+ &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x)
+                  \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\end{align*}
+On \(|z|\le2c\), the stable-kernel estimates and the top-quotient
+continuity used in \eqref{eq:abstract-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded
+modulus \(\omega_c(t)\to0\) such that the Taylor remainder has combined
+\(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norm at most
+\(\omega_c(|z|)|z|^r\).  Dominated convergence against \(|x|^r\) controls
+the first line.  On the support of \(\chi_s\),
+\(|x|\ge cs\), and the mode bounds give, for \(1\le j\le r\),
+\[
+ \left\|\int\chi_s(x)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|\int\chi_s(x)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
+ \le C_cs^{-r}\int_{|x|\ge cs}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+Hence
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:convention-remainder-smallness}
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
+ \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}),
+ \qquad \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r}).
+\end{equation}
+
+The retained potential is nonnegative and has mass
+\(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\).  Since the common jet has zero mean,
+\(A_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) has mass one, and
+\[
+ \inf_yA_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-	au_{s,\chi}^\lambda\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+This proves positivity and normalization.  If the retained mass is nonzero,
+convexity of relative entropy and the bounded-score translate estimate yield
+\[
+ \int \frac{V_{s,\chi}^\lambda}{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \log\frac{V_{s,\chi}^\lambda}{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
+ \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+ \int\chi_s(x)\{C+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The finite \(r\)-th moment, hence finite first moment, proves the last
+inequality.  Adding the bounded common core preserves finite relative
+entropy.  The zero retained-mass case is immediate.
+
+Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:two-background-kl-perturbation} to
+\eqref{eq:convention-exact-tail-split}.  The two backgrounds tend to one in
+\(L^1\), their difference is bounded by the two tail masses and is therefore
+\(o(s^{-r})\), and \eqref{eq:convention-remainder-smallness} supplies the
+required remainders.  The difference of the order-\(r\) modes is
+\(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\).  The lemma gives the displayed entropy
+expansion for every additive hard or smooth convention.  Subtracting two
+such expansions proves their equivalence modulo \(o(s^{-2r})\).
+
+For the normalization comparison, set
+\[
+ X_{s,t}^\lambda=
+ \frac{A_{s,\chi}^\lambda+t\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
+      {1+t\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda},\qquad 0\le t\le1.
+\]
+The endpoints are the additive and multiplicative proxies.  The preceding
+entropy bound and \(\log(1+u)\le C_cu^r\) for \(u\ge c\) imply, uniformly in
+\(t\),
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(X_{s,t}^\nu\|X_{s,t}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}),
+ \qquad
+ \|X_{s,t}^\nu-X_{s,t}^\eta\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+Differentiating the relative entropy along this interpolation, using the
+common positive lower bound and
+\(\partial_tX_{s,t}^\lambda=
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda(1-X_{s,t}^\lambda)/
+ (1+t\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda)\), shows that its derivative is
+\(o(s^{-2r})\) uniformly on \([0,1]\).  Truncation of the retained
+potentials justifies differentiation, and the displayed translate-entropy
+bound permits passage to the limit.  Integration in \(t\) proves that the
+two normalizations differ by \(o(s^{-2r})\), completing the proof.
+\end{proof}

Finally,\n\\[\n \\beta(1-1/q)\\le p,\\qquad m\\le p<m+1,\n\\]\nwith equality in the first relation when \\(\\beta>4\\).  These observations\nprove \\eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Critical Bregman perturbation bound]\n\\label{lem:critical-lq-kl-perturbation}\nLet \\(1<q\\le2\\) and\n\\(\\Phi(s)=(1+s)\\log(1+s)-s\\) on \\([-1,\\infty)\\), with\n\\(0\\log0=0\\).  There is a constant \\(C_q\\) such that\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-bregman-pointwise-bound}\n 0\\le \\Phi(u+v)-\\Phi(u)-\\log(1+u)v\\le C_q|v|^q\n\\end{equation}\nwhenever \\(|u|\\le1/4\\) and \\(u+v\\ge-1\\).\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe lower bound is convexity.  If \\(|v|\\le1/2\\), the segment between\n\\(u\\) and \\(u+v\\) is contained in \\([-3/4,3/4]\\).  Since\n\\(\\Phi\'\'(s)=(1+s)^{-1}\\) there, Taylor\'s theorem gives an upper bound\n\\(C v^2\\le C|v|^q\\).  If \\(v<-1/2\\), the admissible pairs\n\\((u,v)\\) range over a compact set and \\(|v|^q\\ge2^{-q}\\); continuity at\n\\(u+v=-1\\) gives the result.  If \\(v>1/2\\), direct expansion of the left\nside shows that it is at most \\(C(1+v)\\log(1+v)+Cv\\), which is bounded by\n\\(C_qv^q\\).  These three regions prove\n\\eqref{eq:critical-bregman-pointwise-bound}.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{theorem}[Optimal uniform sufficient moment exponent for stable KL asymptotics]\n\\label{thm:high-dimensional-kl-moment-threshold}\nLet \\(d\\ge1\\), \\(0<\\alpha<2\\), and let \\(\\nu\\) be a probability law on\n\\(\\RR^d\\) with mean \\(\\bar\\gamma\\).  Put\n\\(X=\\gamma-\\bar\\gamma\\), and assume\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-kl-moment-hypothesis}\n \\EE|X|^{p_{\\alpha,d}}<\\infty,\n \\qquad\n p_{\\alpha,d}=\\max\\left\\{2,\n \\frac{4(d+\\alpha)}{d+\\alpha+4}\\right\\},\n\\end{equation}\nthen the covariance \\(\\Sigma=\\EE[XX^{\\mathsf T}]\\) is finite and\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-kl-leading-asymptotic}\n H_{\\alpha,d}(s):=\n D_{\\rm KL}\\!\\left(p_s^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\nu\\,\\middle\\|\\,\n p_s^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\mathord\\cdot-\\bar\\gamma)\\right)\n =\\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)s^{-4}+o(s^{-4}),\n\\end{equation}\nwhere\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:stable-leading-covariance-functional}\n b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}(y)\n :=\\frac1{2p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)}\n   \\sum_{i,j=1}^d\\Sigma_{ij}\\partial_{ij}p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y),\n \\qquad\n \\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)\n :=\\frac12\\int b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}^2\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}.\n\\end{equation}\nThe exponent is optimal only in the following uniform sense.  For every\n\\(0<r<2\\), there is a mean-zero law with finite \\(r\\)th absolute moment\nand \\(\\limsup_{s\\to\\infty}s^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s)=+\\infty\\).  If\n\\(d+\\alpha>4\\), then for every \\(2\\le r<p_{\\alpha,d}\\) the counterexample\nmay additionally be chosen with positive-definite finite covariance.\nThus no smaller moment exponent implies\n\\eqref{eq:critical-kl-leading-asymptotic} uniformly over its entire moment\nclass, and the endpoint belongs to the sufficient side.\n\nThis is not a law-by-law moment criterion.  When \\(d+\\alpha>4\\), finite\n\\(p_{\\alpha,d}\\)-moment is not asserted to be necessary for an individual\nlaw; the exact finite-covariance criterion is the nonlinear raw-tail energy\nin Theorem~\\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} below.  When\n\\(d+\\alpha\\le4\\), the exponent is two and boundedness of\n\\(s^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s)\\) does force finite covariance, as the proof below\nshows.  For \\(\\alpha=1\\) with the standard normalization\n\\(p_1^{(1,d)}=P_1^{(d)}\\), one has\n\\(\\mathcal Q_{1,d}=\\mathcal Q_d\\), so the theorem contains the radial\nPoisson result above.\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nTranslation permits us to assume \\(\\bar\\gamma=0\\).  Fix\n\\(q=q_{\\alpha,d}\\), \\(p=p_{\\alpha,d}\\), and \\(m=\\lfloor p\\rfloor\\),\nand write\n\\[\n R_m(y,z)=F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(y,z),\n \\qquad r_s(y)=\\EE R_m(y,X/s).\n\\]\nMinkowski\'s inequality and\n\\eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder} give\n\\[\n s^p\\|R_m(\\cdot,X/s)\\|_q\\le C_{\\alpha,d}|X|^p.\n\\]\nFor each fixed \\(X\\), the local part of the same estimate and \\(m+1>p\\)\ngive\n\\[\n s^p\\|R_m(\\cdot,X/s)\\|_q\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d}|X|^{m+1}s^{p-m-1}\\longrightarrow0.\n\\]\nDominated convergence therefore yields\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-lq-integrated-remainder}\n \\|r_s\\|_{L^q(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-p}).\n\\end{equation}\n\nCentering removes the linear Taylor layer.  Averaging the remaining layers\ngives\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-kl-quotient-decomposition}\n \\delta_s^{(\\alpha,d)}=u_s+r_s,\n \\qquad\n u_s=s^{-2}b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}\n       +\\mathbf 1_{\\{m=3\\}}s^{-3}B_3,\n\\end{equation}\nwhere \\(B_3\\) is a bounded linear combination of third-order modes.  In the\nsecond case the required third moments exist because \\(p\\ge3\\).  Hence\n\\(\\|u_s\\|_\\infty=O(s^{-2})\\).  The boundedness of all these modes follows\nfrom Proposition~\\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}.\n\nThe identity\n\\(F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}(\\dd y)\n=p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y-z)\\dd y\\) shows that every translated quotient has\nintegral one.  Moreover,\n\\(\\int|F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-1|\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}(\\dd y)\\le2\\), so Tonelli\'s\ntheorem gives \\(\\delta_s^{(\\alpha,d)}\\in L^1(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})\\) with\nzero integral.  The KL change of variables is therefore\n\\[\n H_{\\alpha,d}(s)=\\int\\Phi(\\delta_s^{(\\alpha,d)})\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\n\\]\nin the extended sense.  For all sufficiently large \\(s\\), apply\nLemma~\\ref{lem:critical-lq-kl-perturbation} to \\(u=u_s\\), \\(v=r_s\\).\nHölder\'s inequality and \\eqref{eq:critical-lq-integrated-remainder} give\n\\begin{align*}\n \\left|H_{\\alpha,d}(s)-\\int\\Phi(u_s)\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\\right|\n &\\le \\|\\log(1+u_s)\\|_{q/(q-1)}\\|r_s\\|_q\n       +C_q\\|r_s\\|_q^q\\\\\n &\\le O(s^{-2})o(s^{-p})+o(s^{-pq})=o(s^{-4}),\n\\end{align*}\nbecause \\(p\\ge2\\) and \\(pq=4\\).\nThis estimate also proves that the extended KL integral is finite for all\nsufficiently large \\(s\\).\n\nFinally, the boundedness of the retained modes permits a uniform Taylor\nexpansion of \\(\\Phi(u_s)\\).  From\n\\eqref{eq:critical-kl-quotient-decomposition},\n\\[\n \\int\\Phi(u_s)\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\n =\\frac{s^{-4}}2\\int b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}^2\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\n   +o(s^{-4})\n =\\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)s^{-4}+o(s^{-4}),\n\\]\nwhich proves \\eqref{eq:critical-kl-leading-asymptotic}.\n\nWe first prove the obstruction below two moments.  If\n\\(\\limsup_{s\\to\\infty}s^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s)<\\infty\\), Pinsker\'s inequality\nand scaling give, for every fixed \\(\\xi\\in\\RR^d\\),\n\\[\n |\\widehat p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\xi)|\n |\\varphi_X(\\xi/s)-1|\n \\le \\|p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\nu_s-p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}\\|_1\n \\le \\sqrt{2H_{\\alpha,d}(s)}=O(s^{-2}),\n\\]\nwhere \\(\\nu_s\\) is the law of \\(X/s\\).  Since the stable characteristic\nfunction never vanishes, take \\(\\xi=e\\) for a unit vector \\(e\\), multiply\nthe real part by \\(s^2\\), and use Fatou\'s lemma to obtain\n\\[\n \\frac12\\EE(e\\cdot X)^2\n \\le \\liminf_{s\\to\\infty}s^2\n       \\EE[1-\\cos((e\\cdot X)/s)]<\\infty.\n\\]\nThus bounded scaled entropy forces finite covariance.  Given \\(0<r<2\\),\nchoose \\(a\\in(\\max\\{1,r\\},2)\\) and put symmetric masses proportional to\n\\(n^{-a-1}\\) at \\(\\pm ne_1\\), with the remaining mass at zero. Boundedness of the modes follows again from\nProposition~\\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Two-background critical Bregman transfer]\n\\label{lem:two-background-critical-bregman-transfer}\nLet \\(1<q\\le2\\), \\(p\\ge r>0\\), and \\(pq=2r\\). In particular,\nit is invariant under a simultaneous translation of the original law and\nits matched reference.\n\n\\begin{theorem}[First-channel closure and the even-moment hierarchy]\n\\label{thm:first-cayley-mode-closure}\nLet \\(\\nu\\) be a probability law on \\(\\RR\\) with finite mean, and use the\nCayley coordinate\n\\[\n z=\\frac{1+\\ii y}{1-\\ii y}\\in\\TT\\setminus\\{-1\\}.\n\\]\nThen, for every \\(t>0\\),\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:first-channel-exact-fourier-series}\n \\frac{(P_t*\\nu)(\\bar\\gamma+ty)}{P_t(ty)}\n =1+\\sum_{k\\ge1}\n \\bigl(\\overline{c_k(t)}z^k+c_k(t)z^{-k}\\bigr).\n\\end{equation}\nThe series converges pointwise for every \\(y\\in\\RR\\), locally uniformly in\n\\(y\\), and in \\(L^2(\\omega)\\) whenever \\(\\EE X^2<\\infty\\).  Its coefficients\nsatisfy the exact differential closure\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:first-channel-differential-closure}\n c_{k+1}(t)=-c_k(t)-\\frac{t}{k}c_k\'(t),\n \\qquad k\\ge1.\n\\end{equation}\nConsequently, the scale trajectory \\(c_1\\), with its successive derivatives,\ndetermines the matched quotient of the centred law at every scale.  Under\nfinite variance one also has\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:first-channel-chi-square-parseval}\n \\chi^2\\!\\left(P_t*\\nu\\,\\middle\\|\\,\n P_t(\\mathord\\cdot-\\bar\\gamma)\\right)\n =2\\sum_{k\\ge1}|c_k(t)|^2.\n\\end{equation}\nIf \\(\\varphi_X(s)=\\EE e^{\\ii sX}\\), then\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:first-channel-laplace-resolvent}\n \\frac{1+c_1(t)}{2t}\n =\\EE\\frac1{2t-\\ii X}\n =\\int_0^\\infty e^{-2ts}\\varphi_X(s)\\,\\dd s.\n\\end{equation}\nThus the full scale trajectory identifies the centred law by the classical\nuniqueness of the Laplace and characteristic transforms. Differentiation under the\nexpectation proves \\eqref{eq:first-channel-differential-closure}.\n\nAlso \\(1+a_t(X)=2t/(2t-\\ii X)\\). The right side of\n\\eqref{eq:first-channel-even-moment-remainder} increases pointwise with\n\\(t\\), so monotone convergence proves the final assertion.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\subsection{The infinite critical-moment boundary is not spectrally identifiable}\n\nThe finite critical-moment theorem below cannot be extended by replacing its\nmoment hypothesis with vague multivariate regular variation at the same\nindex.  We use the standard measure formulation of multivariate regular\nvariation on \\(\\RR^d\\setminus\\{0\\}\\), as in\nHult--Lindskog~\\cite{HultLindskog2006RegularVariation}.  For a probability\nmeasure \\(\\sigma\\) on \\(S^{d-1}\\) and \\(p>0\\), write\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-rv-tail-measure}\n \\mu_\\sigma(\\dd\\rho,\\dd\\theta)\n =p\\rho^{-p-1}\\dd\\rho\\,\\sigma(\\dd\\theta).\n\\end{equation}\n\nWe first record a lower bound which requires no regular-variation\nhypothesis.\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Finite-covariance Fatou lower bound]\n\\label{lem:finite-covariance-fatou-lower-bound}\nLet \\(d\\ge1\\), and let \\(\\nu\\) be a centred probability law on \\(\\RR^d\\)\nwith finite covariance matrix \\(\\Sigma\\).  Then, with the relative entropy\nunderstood in the extended sense,\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:finite-covariance-fatou-lower-bound}\n \\liminf_{t\\to\\infty}t^4H_d(t)\\ge \\mathcal Q_d(\\Sigma).\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nFix \\(y\\in\\RR^d\\).  Taylor\'s formula near the origin, followed by the\nelementary large-\\(z\\) bound, gives\n\\[\n \\left|F_y(z)-1-D_zF_y(0)z\\right|\\le C_y|z|^2,\n \\qquad z\\in\\RR^d.\n\\]\nIndeed, the assertion is the usual second-order Taylor bound for\n\\(|z|\\le1\\); for \\(|z|>1\\), \\(F_y(z)\\le(1+|y|^2)^{(d+1)/2}\\), while the\nsubtracted affine function is \\(O_y(1+|z|)\\).  Centering and dominated\nconvergence therefore imply\n\\[\n t^2\\delta_t^{(d)}(y)\\longrightarrow b_\\Sigma(y).\n\\]\nSince \\(\\Phi\\ge0\\) on \\([-1,\\infty)\\) and\n\\(t^4\\Phi(\\delta_t^{(d)}(y))\\to b_\\Sigma(y)^2/2\\), Fatou\'s lemma yields\n\\[\n \\liminf_{t\\to\\infty}t^4H_d(t)\n \\ge \\frac12\\int_{\\RR^d}b_\\Sigma^2\\dd\\Omega_d\n =\\mathcal Q_d(\\Sigma),\n\\]\nwhere the last identity is Theorem~\\ref{thm:multidim-covariance-algebra}.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{theorem}[Critical vague tails do not identify the leading entropy]\n\\label{thm:critical-vague-tail-nonidentifiability}\nFix \\(d\\ge4\\), and set\n\\[\n p=\\frac{4(d+1)}{d+5},\\qquad\n q=\\frac{d+5}{d+1}=1+\\frac4{d+1};\n\\]\nthus \\(pq=4\\).  Let \\(\\sigma\\) be normalized surface measure on\n\\(S^{d-1}\\), and let \\(L(r)=\\log r\\).  For every positive-definite matrix\n\\(\\Sigma\\), there are two centred probability laws\n\\(\\nu_{\\rm ac}\\) and \\(\\nu_{\\rm cl}\\) with covariance \\(\\Sigma\\) such that\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-vague-tail-common-limit}\n \\frac{r^p}{\\log r}\\,\\nu_\\bullet(r\\,\\mathord\\cdot)\n \\xrightarrow[r\\to\\infty]{v}\\mu_\\sigma\n \\quad\\text{on }\\RR^d\\setminus\\{0\\},\n \\qquad \\bullet\\in\\{\\mathrm{ac},\\mathrm{cl}\\},\n\\end{equation}\nbut\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-vague-tail-contrasting-entropy}\n t^4H_{d,{\\rm ac}}(t)\\longrightarrow\\mathcal Q_d(\\Sigma),\n \\qquad\n \\limsup_{t\\to\\infty}t^4H_{d,{\\rm cl}}(t)=+\\infty.\n\\end{equation}\nConsequently, the spectral measure and the slowly varying factor do not\ndetermine whether the covariance lower bound is an asymptotic equality,\neven when the spectral measure is smooth, everywhere nondegenerate, and\nantipodally symmetric.\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nWe construct the tails first and then complete them on a bounded set.  Choose\n\\(s_1\\) large and put \\(R_0=e^{s_1}\\).  The diffuse tail is\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-diffuse-tail-definition}\n \\tau_{\\rm ac}(\\dd r,\\dd\\theta)\n =p r^{-p-1}\\log r\\,\\mathbf1_{\\{r\\ge R_0\\}}\n   \\dd r\\,\\sigma(\\dd\\theta).\n\\end{equation}\nChanging variables \\(r=R\\rho\\) and applying dominated convergence against\neach compactly supported continuous test function on\n\\(\\RR^d\\setminus\\{0\\}\\) proves\n\\(R^p(\\log R)^{-1}\\tau_{\\rm ac}(R\\,\\mathord\\cdot)\\to\\mu_\\sigma\\).\n\nFor the clustered tail, define recursively\n\\[\n s_{n+1}=s_n+s_n^{-1/2},\\qquad R_n=e^{s_n},\\qquad\n W_n=\\int_{s_n}^{s_{n+1}}pu e^{-pu}\\dd u.\n\\]\nChoose an antipodally symmetric equal-weight empirical probability\n\\(\\pi_n\\) on \\(S^{d-1}\\), supported on\n\\(N_n\\asymp s_n^{1/4}\\) points, so that \\(\\pi_n\\Rightarrow\\sigma\\), and set\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-clustered-tail-definition}\n \\tau_{\\rm cl}=\\sum_{n\\ge1}W_n(\\theta\\mapsto R_n\\theta)_\\#\\pi_n.\n\\end{equation}\nThis tail has the same vague limit.  To verify the assertion without a\nmoving-set argument, let \\(f\\in C_c(\\RR^d\\setminus\\{0\\})\\) and write\n\\(R=e^s\\).  Then\n\\[\n \\frac{e^{ps}}s\\int f(x/e^s)\\tau_{\\rm cl}(\\dd x)\n =\\frac{e^{ps}}s\\sum_nW_n\n   \\int f(e^{s_n-s}\\theta)\\pi_n(\\dd\\theta).\n\\]\nOnly indices with \\(s_n-s\\) in a fixed compact interval occur.  On this\ninterval the maximal mesh \\(s_n^{-1/2}\\) tends to zero, \\(u/s\\to1\\)\nuniformly, and \\(\\pi_n\\Rightarrow\\sigma\\) uniformly over the indices in\nquestion.  The right side is therefore a Riemann sum converging to\n\\[\n \\int_\\RR pe^{-pv}\\int_{S^{d-1}}f(e^v\\theta)\n \\sigma(\\dd\\theta)\\dd v\n =\\int f\\dd\\mu_\\sigma.\n\\]\nThis proves \\eqref{eq:critical-vague-tail-common-limit} for the two tails.\n\nBoth tails have arbitrarily small total mass and covariance when \\(s_1\\) is\nlarge, because \\(p>2\\).  They are symmetric.  After increasing \\(s_1\\),\ntheir covariance matrices \\(C_\\bullet\\) satisfy\n\\(C_\\bullet<\\Sigma\\).  A bounded symmetric measure of the remaining mass\ncan realize the covariance \\(\\Sigma-C_\\bullet\\): diagonalize that matrix\nand place equal pairs of atoms on its eigenvectors with the corresponding\nradii.  Thus each tail can be completed to a centred probability law with\ncovariance exactly \\(\\Sigma\\), without changing its vague limit.\n\nWe next prove the diffuse asymptotic.  Let\n\\(m=2\\) when \\(p\\le3\\) and \\(m=3\\) when \\(p>3\\).  The local Taylor estimate\n\\eqref{eq:local-multidim-taylor-remainder}, the boundedness of the retained\nmodes, and symmetry give\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-diffuse-quotient-remainder}\n \\|r_t\\|_\\infty+\\|r_t\\|_{L^1(\\Omega_d)}\n \\le C\\left\\{\n t^{-(m+1)}\\EE[|X|^{m+1};|X|\\le t]+t^{-p}\\log t\n \\right\\},\n\\end{equation}\nwhere\n\\(\\delta_t^{(d)}=t^{-2}b_\\Sigma+r_t\\).  For completeness, the only\nestimate in \\eqref{eq:critical-diffuse-quotient-remainder} not already\ncontained in the local Taylor bound is the uniform control of the diffuse\ntail.  In Lebesgue coordinates it follows from\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-diffuse-convolution-bound}\n \\sup_{y\\in\\RR^d}\\int_{|z|>1}F_y(z)|z|^{-d-p}\n (1+\\log|z|)\\dd z<\\infty.\n\\end{equation}\nFor \\(|y|\\le2\\) the bound is immediate.  If \\(|y|=R>2\\), split the\nintegral into \\(|z-y|\\le R/2\\) and its complement.  In the first region\n\\(|z|\\asymp R\\), and translation by \\(y\\) bounds the integral by\n\\(CR^{1-p}(1+\\log R)\\); in the second region \\(F_y(z)\\le C_d\\), and the\nradial weight is integrable.  Since \\(p>1\\), this proves\n\\eqref{eq:critical-diffuse-convolution-bound}.  Integration in \\(y\\) uses\n\\(\\int F_y(z)\\Omega_d(\\dd y)=1\\), and gives the corresponding \\(L^1\\)\nbound.  The polynomial tail terms are bounded by the same\n\\(O(t^{-p}\\log t)\\) quantity because \\(m<p\\), proving\n\\eqref{eq:critical-diffuse-quotient-remainder}.\n\nWhen \\(p\\ne3\\), the right side of\n\\eqref{eq:critical-diffuse-quotient-remainder} is\n\\(O(t^{-p}\\log t)=o(t^{-2})\\).  At the sole integer endpoint \\(p=3\\),\nequivalently \\(d=11\\), its first term is\n\\(O(t^{-3}(\\log t)^2)=o(t^{-2})\\).  The second-order quotient criterion,\nTheorem~\\ref{thm:second-order-quotient-kl-coefficient}, now gives the first\nlimit in \\eqref{eq:critical-vague-tail-contrasting-entropy}.  Notice also\nthat the whole construction is antipodally symmetric; at \\(d=11\\) every\ntruncated third-moment tensor is therefore identically zero.\n\nIt remains to obtain the clustered lower bound.  Each atom in the \\(n\\)th\nshell has mass\n\\[\n a_n=\\frac{W_n}{N_n}\\sim p s_n^{1/4}R_n^{-p},\n \\qquad R_n^pa_n\\longrightarrow\\infty.\n\\]\nFix one such atom, choose a sufficiently small constant \\(\\kappa>0\\), and\nput\n\\[\n t_n=\\kappa R_na_n^{1/(d+1)}.\n\\]\nThen \\(t_n\\to\\infty\\) and \\(t_n/R_n\\to0\\).  If \\(A_n\\) is the ball of\nradius \\(t_n\\) centred at that atom, the corresponding mixture component\nand the centred reference satisfy\n\\[\n (P_{t_n}^{(d)}*\\nu_{\\rm cl})(A_n)\\ge c_da_n,\n \\qquad\n P_{t_n}^{(d)}(A_n)\\le C_d(t_n/R_n)^{d+1}\n =C_d\\kappa^{d+1}a_n.\n\\]\nChoose \\(\\kappa\\) so that the second constant is smaller by a fixed factor.\nData processing to \\(\\{A_n,A_n^c\\}\\), followed by\n\\(D(\\operatorname{Ber}(u)\\|\\operatorname{Ber}(v))\n\\ge u\\log(u/v)-u+v\\), gives \\(H_{d,{\\rm cl}}(t_n)\\ge c\'_da_n\\).\nConsequently,\n\\[\n t_n^4H_{d,{\\rm cl}}(t_n)\n \\ge c_dR_n^4a_n^{1+4/(d+1)}\n =c_d(R_n^pa_n)^q\n \\asymp s_n^{q/4}\\longrightarrow\\infty,\n\\]\nwhere \\(pq=4\\).  This proves the second limit and the theorem.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\subsection{Moment-matched comparisons and Gaussian compression}\n\nFor a probability law \\(\\rho\\) with a finite \\(j\\)th absolute moment, write\n\\(m_j(\\rho)=\\int x^j\\rho(\\dd x)\\).  The comparison theorem below does not\nrequire either law to be centred.\n\n\\begin{theorem}[First unmatched moment for Poisson relative entropy]\n\\label{thm:moment-matched-poisson-kl}\nLet \\(r\\ge2\\), and let \\(\\nu,\\eta\\) be probability laws on \\(\\RR\\) with\nfinite \\(r\\)th absolute moments.  Suppose\n\\[\n m_j(\\nu)=m_j(\\eta)\\quad(0\\le j<r),\n \\qquad \\Delta_r:=m_r(\\nu)-m_r(\\eta)\\ne0.\n\\]\nThen\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:moment-matched-poisson-kl}\n D_{\\rm KL}(P_t*\\nu\\|P_t*\\eta)\n =C_r\\Delta_r^2t^{-2r}+o(t^{-2r}),\n \\qquad\n C_r=4^{-r}\\binom{2r-2}{r-1}.\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nDivide both smoothed densities by \\(P_t(ty)\\), and denote the resulting\nquotients by \\(q_t^\\nu\\) and \\(q_t^\\eta\\).  The global two-region Taylor\nremainder \\eqref{eq:one-dimensional-two-region-taylor-remainder}, applied\nat order \\(r\\), gives\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:moment-matched-quotient-difference}\n q_t^\\nu-q_t^\\eta\n =\\Delta_r u_r t^{-r}+o(t^{-r})\n \\quad\\text{in }L^\\infty(\\omega)\\cap L^1(\\omega).\n\\end{equation}\nThe same argument at order one shows \\(q_t^\\eta\\to1\\) uniformly.  Since the\ntwo quotient differences have zero \\(\\omega\\)-mean, the exact Bregman form is\n\\[\n D_{\\rm KL}(P_t*\\nu\\|P_t*\\eta)\n =\\int q_t^\\eta\n \\Phi\\!\\left(\\frac{q_t^\\nu-q_t^\\eta}{q_t^\\eta}\\right)\\dd\\omega.\n\\]\nUniform Taylor expansion of \\(\\Phi(s)=s^2/2+O(s^3)\\), together with\n\\eqref{eq:moment-matched-quotient-difference}, yields\n\\[\n D_{\\rm KL}(P_t*\\nu\\|P_t*\\eta)\n =\\frac{\\Delta_r^2}{2}t^{-2r}\\int u_r^2\\dd\\omega+o(t^{-2r}).\n\\]\nBy the Laurent coefficient formula\n\\eqref{eq:mode-laurent-coefficients} and Parseval,\n\\[\n \\frac12\\int u_r^2\\dd\\omega\n =4^{-r}\\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}\\binom{r-1}{j}^2\n =4^{-r}\\binom{2r-2}{r-1},\n\\]\nwhere the last equality is Vandermonde\'s identity.\n\\end{proof}\n\nWe now state the Gaussian quadrature consequence with the nondegeneracy\nhypothesis made explicit.  This qualification is necessary: an \\(n\\)-node\nquadrature rule is not defined for an arbitrary law supported on fewer than\n\\(n\\) points.\n\n\\begin{theorem}[Gaussian-comparison entropy threshold]\n\\label{thm:gauss-poisson-kl-threshold}\nLet \\(n\\ge1\\), and let \\(\\nu\\) be a probability law on \\(\\RR\\) satisfying\n\\[\n \\EE|X|^{2n-1}<\\infty,\n \\qquad |\\operatorname{supp}\\nu|\\ge n.\n\\]\nLet \\(\\pi_n\\) be the monic degree-\\(n\\) polynomial orthogonal to\n\\(1,x,\\ldots,x^{n-1}\\) with respect to \\(\\nu\\), and let \\(G_n\\nu\\) be its\n\\(n\\)-node Gaussian quadrature law.  Thus\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:gauss-moment-matching}\n m_j(G_n\\nu)=m_j(\\nu),\\qquad 0\\le j\\le2n-1.\n\\end{equation}\nThen\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:gauss-poisson-finite-limit}\n \\EE|X|^{2n}<\\infty\n \\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad\n \\lim_{t\\to\\infty}t^{4n}\n D_{\\rm KL}(P_t*\\nu\\|P_t*G_n\\nu)\n =4^{-2n}\\binom{4n-2}{2n-1}\n \\|\\pi_n\\|_{L^2(\\nu)}^4,\n\\end{equation}\nwhereas\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:gauss-poisson-infinite-limit}\n \\EE|X|^{2n}=\\infty\n \\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad\n t^{4n}D_{\\rm KL}(P_t*\\nu\\|P_t*G_n\\nu)\\longrightarrow+\\infty.\n\\end{equation}\nConsequently,\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:gauss-poisson-moment-equivalence}\n \\EE|X|^{2n}<\\infty\n \\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n \\limsup_{t\\to\\infty}t^{4n}\n D_{\\rm KL}(P_t*\\nu\\|P_t*G_n\\nu)<\\infty.\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe existence, positivity, and exactness\n\\eqref{eq:gauss-moment-matching} of the Gaussian rule are classical; see\n\\cite{GolubWelsch1969GaussQuadrature}.  If the \\(2n\\)th moment is finite,\nthen, because \\(\\pi_n\\) vanishes at every quadrature node and\n\\(\\pi_n^2-x^{2n}\\) has degree at most \\(2n-1\\),\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:gauss-missing-moment-norm}\n m_{2n}(\\nu)-m_{2n}(G_n\\nu)\n =\\int\\pi_n^2\\dd\\nu=\\|\\pi_n\\|_{L^2(\\nu)}^2.\n\\end{equation}\nTheorem~\\ref{thm:moment-matched-poisson-kl}, with \\(r=2n\\), now proves\n\\eqref{eq:gauss-poisson-finite-limit}.  If the norm in\n\\eqref{eq:gauss-missing-moment-norm} vanishes, then \\(\\nu\\) is itself\nsupported on the Gaussian nodes and both sides of\n\\eqref{eq:gauss-poisson-finite-limit} are zero.\n\nSuppose instead that \\(\\EE|X|^{2n}=\\infty\\).  Apply\n\\eqref{eq:first-channel-even-moment-remainder} to \\(\\nu\\) and to the\nfinite-support law \\(G_n\\nu\\).  Their even moments through order \\(2n-2\\)\nagree, and therefore\n\\[\n t^{2n}\\left|\\Re\\{c_1^\\nu(t)-c_1^{G_n\\nu}(t)\\}\\right|\n \\longrightarrow+\\infty.\n\\]\nThe real part of \\(z\\) is a bounded test of norm one on the Cayley circle.\nPinsker\'s inequality and the Fourier coefficient identity therefore give\n\\[\n 2D_{\\rm KL}(P_t*\\nu\\|P_t*G_n\\nu)\n \\ge\\left|\\Re\\{c_1^\\nu(t)-c_1^{G_n\\nu}(t)\\}\\right|^2.\n\\]\nMultiplication by \\(t^{4n}\\) proves\n\\eqref{eq:gauss-poisson-infinite-limit}, and the equivalence follows.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{remark}[Classical optimal degree]\nThe assertion that an \\(n\\)-node positive quadrature rule has maximal exact\ndegree \\(2n-1\\), and that Gaussian quadrature attains this degree, is a\nclassical quadrature theorem, not a new result of this article.  The node\npolynomial gives the elementary obstruction at degree \\(2n\\); see\n\\cite{GolubWelsch1969GaussQuadrature}.\n\\end{remark}\n\n\\begin{corollary}[Two-node fourth-moment coefficient]\n\\label{cor:two-node-gauss-fourth-moment}\nAssume\n\\[\n \\EE X=0,\\qquad \\EE X^2=1,\\qquad \\EE|X|^3<\\infty,\n\\]\nand put\n\\[\n \\beta_3=\\EE X^3,\\qquad\n \\pi_2(x)=x^2-\\beta_3x-1.\n\\]\nLet \\(G_2\\nu\\) be the two-node Gaussian quadrature law.  If\n\\(\\EE X^4<\\infty\\), then, with\n\\[\n \\kappa=\\|\\pi_2\\|_{L^2(\\nu)}^2\n =\\EE X^4-1-\\beta_3^2,\n\\]\none has\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:two-node-fourth-moment-coefficient}\n \\lim_{t\\to\\infty}t^8D_{\\rm KL}(P_t*\\nu\\|P_t*G_2\\nu)\n =\\frac5{64}\\kappa^2.\n\\end{equation}\nIf \\(\\EE X^4=\\infty\\), the left side of\n\\eqref{eq:two-node-fourth-moment-coefficient} tends to \\(+\\infty\\).  For a\nsymmetric law,\n\\(G_2\\nu=(\\delta_{-1}+\\delta_1)/2\\) and\n\\(\\kappa=\\EE X^4-1\\).\n\\end{corollary}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe polynomial \\(\\pi_2\\) is monic and orthogonal to \\(1,x\\).  Its squared\nnorm is the identity proved in Lemma ``Normalized\nfourth-moment defect algebra.\'\'  Apply\nTheorem~\\ref{thm:gauss-poisson-kl-threshold} and use\n\\(4^{-4}\\binom63=5/64\\).  In the symmetric case, exactness through degree\nthree and unit variance force the nodes and weights to be\n\\(\\{-1,1\\}\\) and \\(\\{1/2,1/2\\}\\).\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{theorem}[Square boundary at a missing Gaussian moment]\n\\label{thm:gauss-regular-variation-square-law}\nLet \\(n\\ge2\\), put \\(p=2n\\), and let \\(\\nu\\) satisfy the hypotheses of\nTheorem~\\ref{thm:gauss-poisson-kl-threshold}.  Assume, for an eventually\npositive slowly varying function \\(L\\) and constants \\(c_+,c_-\\ge0\\) with\n\\(c_++c_->0\\),\n\\[\n \\mathbb P(X>x)\\sim c_+x^{-p}L(x),\\qquad\n \\mathbb P(X<-x)\\sim c_-x^{-p}L(x),\n\\]\nand assume\n\\[\n \\ell_L(t)=\\int_{x_0}^t\\frac{L(s)}s\\dd s\\longrightarrow\\infty.\n\\]\nThen, with\n\\(M_p(t)=\\EE[|X|^p\\mathbf1_{\\{|X|\\le t\\}}]\\),\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:gauss-regular-variation-square-law}\n D_{\\rm KL}(P_t*\\nu\\|P_t*G_n\\nu)\n \\sim C_p t^{-2p}M_p(t)^2,\n \\qquad C_p=4^{-p}\\binom{2p-2}{p-1}.\n\\end{equation}\nIn particular,\n\\[\n M_p(t)\\sim p(c_++c_-)\\ell_L(t),\n\\]\nso the boundary normalization is the square of the integrated slowly\nvarying factor and the leading constant is positive.\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe quotient estimate proved for\nTheorem~\\ref{cor:main-body-conditional-missing-top-moment-tail}, before the\nentropy transfer is applied, gives\n\\[\n q_t^\\nu\n =\\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}m_j(\\nu)u_jt^{-j}\n +u_pt^{-p}M_p(t)+e_t,\n \\qquad\n \\|e_t\\|_\\infty+\\|e_t\\|_{L^1(\\omega)}\n =o(t^{-p}M_p(t)).\n\\]\nThe finite-support law \\(G_n\\nu\\) has an ordinary expansion through order\n\\(p\\), and its moments through order \\(p-1\\) agree with those of \\(\\nu\\).\nSince \\(M_p(t)\\to\\infty\\), subtraction yields\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:gauss-boundary-quotient-difference}\n q_t^\\nu-q_t^{G_n\\nu}\n =u_pt^{-p}M_p(t)+o_{L^\\infty\\cap L^1(\\omega)}\n (t^{-p}M_p(t)).\n\\end{equation}\nInterpolation also gives the same relative error in \\(L^2(\\omega)\\).\nFurthermore \\(q_t^{G_n\\nu}\\to1\\) uniformly.  Applying the Bregman expansion\nfrom the proof of Theorem~\\ref{thm:moment-matched-poisson-kl} to\n\\eqref{eq:gauss-boundary-quotient-difference} gives\n\\[\n D_{\\rm KL}(P_t*\\nu\\|P_t*G_n\\nu)\n =\\frac12t^{-2p}M_p(t)^2\\int u_p^2\\dd\\omega\n +o(t^{-2p}M_p(t)^2).\n\\]\nThe Parseval calculation in that theorem identifies the constant as \\(C_p\\).\nThe asymptotic for \\(M_p\\) is Karamata\'s boundary integral theorem, exactly\nas in Theorem~\\ref{cor:main-body-conditional-missing-top-moment-tail}.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\subsection{The multidimensional \\texorpdfstring{\\(L^2\\)}{L2} and entropy\nthresholds}\n\nWrite \\(a=(d+1)/2\\) and\n\\[\n F_y(z)=\\left(\\frac{1+|y|^2}{1+|y-z|^2}\\right)^a.\n\\]\nLet \\(T_2(y,z)\\) denote the Taylor polynomial of \\(F_y(z)\\) at \\(z=0\\)\nthrough homogeneous degree two.\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Large translations in the Cauchy quotient space]\n\\label{lem:multidim-large-translation-l2-growth}\nFor every \\(d\\ge1\\),\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:translated-quotient-l2-asymptotic}\n \\|F_\\cdot(z)\\|_{L^2(\\Omega_d)}^2\n \\sim2^{-d}|z|^{d+1}\\qquad(|z|\\to\\infty).\n\\end{equation}\nIf\n\\[\n q_d:=\\max\\left\\{2,\\frac{d+1}{2}\\right\\},\n\\]\nthen a constant \\(C_d\\) exists such that\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:second-order-l2-global-remainder}\n \\|F_\\cdot(z)-T_2(\\cdot,z)\\|_{L^2(\\Omega_d)}\n \\le C_d\n \\begin{cases}|z|^3,&|z|\\le1,\\\\ |z|^{q_d},&|z|>1.\n \\end{cases}\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nWith \\(c_d=\\Gamma((d+1)/2)/\\pi^{(d+1)/2}\\) and \\(y=z+u\\),\n\\[\n \\|F_\\cdot(z)\\|_2^2\n =c_d\\int_{\\RR^d}\n \\frac{(1+|z+u|^2)^a}{(1+|u|^2)^{d+1}}\\dd u.\n\\]\nAfter division by \\(|z|^{d+1}\\), dominated convergence applies and gives\n\\[\n c_d\\int_{\\RR^d}(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+1)}\\dd u\n =\\frac{\\Gamma((d+1)/2)\\Gamma(d/2+1)}\n {\\sqrt\\pi\\Gamma(d+1)}=2^{-d}.\n\\]\nFor \\(|z|\\le1\\), differentiation under the \\(L^2(\\Omega_d)\\) norm through\nthird order is uniform on the unit ball, and Taylor\'s formula gives the\nfirst line of \\eqref{eq:second-order-l2-global-remainder}.  For \\(|z|>1\\),\n\\eqref{eq:translated-quotient-l2-asymptotic}, enlarged to a global upper\nbound, and the fact that \\(T_2\\) is a degree-two polynomial in \\(z\\) with\n\\(L^2(\\Omega_d)\\) coefficients give\n\\[\n \\|F_\\cdot(z)-T_2(\\cdot,z)\\|_2\n \\le C_d(|z|^{(d+1)/2}+|z|^2),\n\\]\nwhich is the second line.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{theorem}[Sharp absolute-moment condition for the \\(L^2\\) quotient]\n\\label{thm:multidim-l2-moment-threshold}\nLet \\(\\nu\\) be a centred probability law on \\(\\RR^d\\), with covariance\nmatrix \\(\\Sigma\\).  If\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:multidim-qd-moment}\n \\EE|X|^{q_d}<\\infty,\n \\qquad q_d=\\max\\left\\{2,\\frac{d+1}{2}\\right\\},\n\\end{equation}\nthen\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:multidim-l2-second-order-convergence}\n t^2\\delta_t^{(d)}\\longrightarrow b_\\Sigma\n \\quad\\text{in }L^2(\\Omega_d).\n\\end{equation}\nFor \\(d\\ge4\\), this exponent is sharp among hypotheses stated solely as a\nfinite absolute moment: for every \\(2\\le p<q_d\\), there is a centred law\nwith positive-definite covariance and finite \\(p\\)th absolute moment for\nwhich \\eqref{eq:multidim-l2-second-order-convergence} fails.\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nAfter centering removes the degree-one term and covariance averages the\ndegree-two term, Minkowski\'s inequality gives\n\\[\n \\|t^2\\delta_t^{(d)}-b_\\Sigma\\|_2\n \\le\\EE\\left[t^2\n \\|F_\\cdot(X/t)-T_2(\\cdot,X/t)\\|_2\\right].\n\\]\nThe integrand converges pointwise to zero.  On \\(|X|\\le t\\), the first line\nof \\eqref{eq:second-order-l2-global-remainder} bounds it by \\(C|X|^2\\);\non \\(|X|>t\\), the second line bounds it by\n\\(C|X|^{q_d}t^{2-q_d}\\le C|X|^{q_d}\\).  Dominated convergence proves\n\\eqref{eq:multidim-l2-second-order-convergence}.\n\nFor sharpness, let \\(a=(d+1)/2>2\\), choose \\(p<a\\), and take a symmetric\nspike law with masses \\(w_j/2\\) at \\(\\pm R_je_1\\), where\n\\(w_j=\\alpha_jR_j^{-p}\\), \\(\\sum_j\\alpha_j<\\infty\\), and \\(R_j\\) grows\nrecursively.  Add a sufficiently small bounded symmetric component spanning\n\\(\\RR^d\\).  The resulting law has positive-definite finite covariance and\nfinite \\(p\\)th moment.  Choose\n\\[\n 0<s<\\min\\left\\{\\frac{a-p}{a-2},\\,1-\\frac{p}{d+1}\\right\\}\n\\]\nand put \\(t_j=R_j^s\\).\nOn a fixed ball about \\(R_je_1/t_j\\), the \\(j\\)th translated quotient has\n\\(L^2(\\Omega_d)\\) size comparable to\n\\((R_j/t_j)^a\\), by the localized proof of\n\\eqref{eq:translated-quotient-l2-asymptotic}.  Consequently its contribution\nto \\(t_j^2\\delta_{t_j}^{(d)}\\) has size at least\n\\[\n c\\alpha_jR_j^{a-p-s(a-2)}.\n\\]\nThe first restriction on \\(s\\) makes the displayed exponent positive; the\nsecond gives \\(w_j(R_j/t_j)^{d+1}\\to\\infty\\), so the localized positive spike\nalso dominates the constant background.  Choosing \\(R_j\\) fast enough makes\nthe displayed quantity diverge and dominates the bounded quadratic mode and\nall previously chosen terms.  Hence the \\(L^2\\)\nconvergence fails.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{theorem}[Low-dimensional finite-covariance entropy threshold]\n\n\\label{thm:low-dimensional-finite-covariance-threshold}\nLet \\(1\\le d\\le3\\), and let \\(\\nu\\) be a probability law on \\(\\RR^d\\) with\nfinite mean.  With\n\\[\n H_d(t)=D_{\\rm KL}\\!\\left(P_t^{(d)}*\\nu\\,\\middle\\|\\,\n P_t^{(d)}(\\mathord\\cdot-\\bar\\gamma)\\right),\n\\]\none has\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:low-dimensional-covariance-iff}\n \\EE|X|^2<\\infty\n \\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n \\limsup_{t\\to\\infty}t^4H_d(t)<\\infty.\n\\end{equation}\nIf the covariance is finite, then\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:low-dimensional-covariance-limit}\n H_d(t)=\\mathcal Q_d(\\Sigma)t^{-4}+o(t^{-4}).\n\\end{equation}\nIf it is infinite, then \\(t^4H_d(t)\\to+\\infty\\) in the extended sense.\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nFor \\(d\\le3\\), \\(q_d=2\\).  Thus Theorem\n\\ref{thm:multidim-l2-moment-threshold} and the \\(L^2\\) alternative in\nTheorem~\\ref{thm:second-order-quotient-kl-coefficient} prove\n\\eqref{eq:low-dimensional-covariance-limit}.  The entropy representation is\nvalid in the extended sense by change of variables; for large \\(t\\), the\n\\(L^2\\) convergence makes \\(\\Phi(\\delta_t^{(d)})\\) integrable because\n\\(\\Phi(s)\\le C s^2\\) on \\([-1,\\infty)\\).\n\nConversely, if \\(\\EE|X|^2=\\infty\\), some unit vector \\(e\\) satisfies\n\\(\\EE(e\\cdot X)^2=\\infty\\).  Projection onto \\(e\\) sends the radial\n\\(d\\)-dimensional Poisson law to the one-dimensional Cauchy law at the same\nscale.  The data-processing inequality and\nTheorem~\\ref{thm:sharp-leading-kl-variance-threshold} therefore give\n\\[\n H_d(t)\\ge\n D_{\\rm KL}(P_t*\\nu_e\\|P_t(\\mathord\\cdot-\\bar\\gamma_e)),\n\\]\nwhose product with \\(t^4\\) tends to \\(+\\infty\\).\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{proposition}[Finite covariance does not control high-dimensional KL]\n\\label{prop:high-dimensional-finite-covariance-obstruction}\nFor every \\(d\\ge4\\), there exists a centred discrete probability law on\n\\(\\RR^d\\) with positive-definite finite covariance such that\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:high-dimensional-finite-covariance-obstruction}\n \\limsup_{t\\to\\infty}t^4H_d(t)=+\\infty.\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{proposition}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nChoose positive \\(\\alpha_j\\) with \\(\\sum_j\\alpha_j<\\infty\\), radii\n\\(R_j\\uparrow\\infty\\), and weights\n\\(w_j=\\alpha_jR_j^{-2}\\).  After rescaling the sequence if necessary,\n\\(W=\\sum_jw_j<1\\).  Begin with\n\\[\n (1-W)\\delta_0+\\sum_{j\\ge1}\\frac{w_j}{2}\n (\\delta_{R_je_1}+\\delta_{-R_je_1}),\n\\]\nand transfer an arbitrarily small amount of the mass at zero to a bounded\ncentred symmetric law spanning \\(\\RR^d\\).  The covariance is then positive\ndefinite and finite because \\(\\sum_jw_jR_j^2=\\sum_j\\alpha_j<\\infty\\).\n\nFix a sufficiently small constant \\(\\kappa>0\\), and set\n\\[\n t_j=\\kappa R_jw_j^{1/(d+1)}.\n\\]\nThe radii may be chosen recursively so that \\(t_j\\to\\infty\\).  Let \\(A_j\\)\nbe the ball of radius \\(t_j\\) centred at \\(R_je_1\\).  The \\(j\\)th mixture\ncomponent gives\n\\[\n (P_{t_j}^{(d)}*\\nu)(A_j)\\ge c_dw_j,\n\\]\nwhereas, since \\(t_j/R_j\\to0\\), the centred reference satisfies\n\\[\n P_{t_j}^{(d)}(A_j)\n \\le C_d(t_j/R_j)^{d+1}\n =C_d\\kappa^{d+1}w_j.\n\\]\nChoose \\(\\kappa\\) so that the second constant is strictly smaller than the\nfirst.  Data processing to the partition \\(\\{A_j,A_j^c\\}\\) and\nLemma~\\ref{lem:bernoulli-kl-linear-separation} then give\n\\(H_d(t_j)\\ge c\'_dw_j\\).  Hence\n\\[\n t_j^4H_d(t_j)\n \\ge c\'\'_dR_j^4w_j^{1+4/(d+1)}\n =c\'\'_d\\alpha_j^{1+4/(d+1)}\n R_j^{2(d-3)/(d+1)}.\n\\]\nThe exponent of \\(R_j\\) is positive exactly when \\(d>3\\).  Choosing the\nradii recursively makes the final expression tend to infinity.\n\\end{proof}\n\nFor the high-dimensional entropy topology, define\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-kl-exponents}\n q_d:=\\frac{d+5}{d+1},\n \\qquad\n p_d:=\\frac{4(d+1)}{d+5}.\n\\end{equation}\nThus \\(1<q_d<2\\), \\(2<p_d<4\\), and \\(p_dq_d=4\\) when \\(d\\ge4\\).\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Critical translation remainder]\n\\label{lem:critical-lq-translation-remainder}\nLet \\(d\\ge4\\), let \\(p_d,q_d\\) be as in\n\\eqref{eq:critical-kl-exponents}, and put \\(m=\\lfloor p_d\\rfloor\\).\nIf \\(T_m(y,z)\\) is the Taylor polynomial of \\(F_y(z)\\) through degree\n\\(m\\), then\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-lq-exact-translation-norm}\n \\|F_\\cdot(z)\\|_{L^{q_d}(\\Omega_d)}^{q_d}\n =1+\\frac{2(d+5)}{(d+1)(d+3)}|z|^2\n +\\frac{3}{(d+1)(d+3)}|z|^4.\n\\end{equation}\nConsequently, for a constant depending only on \\(d\\),\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-lq-global-remainder}\n \\|F_\\cdot(z)-T_m(\\cdot,z)\\|_{L^{q_d}(\\Omega_d)}\n \\le C_d\n \\begin{cases}\n |z|^{m+1},& |z|\\le1,\\\\\n |z|^{p_d},& |z|>1,\n \\end{cases}\n \\le C_d|z|^{p_d}.\n\\end{equation}\nHere \\(m=2\\) for \\(4\\le d\\le10\\), while \\(m=3\\) for \\(d\\ge11\\),\nincluding the integer endpoint \\(p_{11}=3\\).\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nSince \\(a(q_d-1)=2\\), translation by \\(z\\) gives\n\\[\n \\|F_\\cdot(z)\\|_{q_d}^{q_d}\n =c_d\\int_{\\RR^d}\n \\frac{(1+|u+z|^2)^2}{(1+|u|^2)^{(d+5)/2}}\\dd u.\n\\]\nWrite \\(A=1+|u|^2\\).  The odd term in the expansion of\n\\((A+|z|^2+2u\\cdot z)^2\\) integrates to zero, and rotational invariance\ngives\n\\[\n \\int(u\\cdot z)^2(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+5)/2}\\dd u\n =\\frac{|z|^2}{d}\\int |u|^2(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+5)/2}\\dd u.\n\\]\nThe three normalized beta integrals needed here are\n\\[\n \\begin{aligned}\n c_d\\int(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}\\dd u&=1,\\\\\n c_d\\int(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+3)/2}\\dd u&=\\frac1{d+1},\\\\\n c_d\\int(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+5)/2}\\dd u\n &=\\frac3{(d+1)(d+3)}.\n \\end{aligned}\n\\]\nSubstitution proves \\eqref{eq:critical-lq-exact-translation-norm}.\n\nFor \\(|z|\\le1\\), the local quotient--Taylor estimate\n\\eqref{eq:local-multidim-taylor-remainder} implies the first line of\n\\eqref{eq:critical-lq-global-remainder}.  For \\(|z|>1\\), the exact identity\ngives \\(\\|F_\\cdot(z)\\|_{q_d}\\le C_d|z|^{4/q_d}=C_d|z|^{p_d}\\).\nEvery coefficient of \\(T_m\\) is bounded in \\(y\\), and \\(m\\le p_d\\), so\n\\(\\|T_m(\\cdot,z)\\|_{q_d}\\le C_d|z|^{p_d}\\).  Finally,\n\\(m+1>p_d\\), which proves the last inequality for \\(|z|\\le1\\).\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\endinput\n\nFor \\(0<\\alpha<2\\), let \\(p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}\\) be the density of any\ncentred isotropic strictly \\(\\alpha\\)-stable law on \\(\\RR^d\\), and use the\nspatial-scale normalization\n\\[\n p_s^{(\\alpha,d)}(x)=s^{-d}p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(x/s),\\qquad s>0.\n\\]\nChanging the scale parameter in the characteristic exponent only changes\nthe choice of \\(p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}\\), so this notation covers every isotropic\nstrictly stable kernel.  Put\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:stable-critical-exponents}\n \\beta=d+\\alpha,\\qquad\n q_{\\alpha,d}:=\\min\\left\\{2,1+\\frac4\\beta\\right\\},\\qquad\n p_{\\alpha,d}:=\\frac4{q_{\\alpha,d}}\n =\\max\\left\\{2,\\frac{4(d+\\alpha)}{d+\\alpha+4}\\right\\}.\n\\end{equation}\nWrite \\(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}(\\dd y)=p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)\\dd y\\) and\n\\[\nF_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)\n:=\\frac{p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y-z)}{p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)}.\n\\]\n\n\\begin{proposition}[Stable-kernel input package]\n\\label{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}\nPut \\(\\beta=d+\\alpha\\).  For every multi-index \\(\\gamma\\), there are positive\nconstants \\(c,C,C_\\gamma\\), depending on \\(d,\\alpha\\) and the chosen stable\nscale, such that\n\\begin{align}\n c(1+|y|)^{-\\beta}&\\le p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)\n \\le C(1+|y|)^{-\\beta},\\label{eq:stable-input-density}\\\\\n |\\partial^\\gamma p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)|\n &\\le C_\\gamma(1+|y|)^{-\\beta-|\\gamma|},\\label{eq:stable-input-derivative}\\\\\n \\frac{|\\partial^\\gamma p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)|}\n {p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)}\n &\\le C_\\gamma(1+|y|)^{-|\\gamma|}.\n \\label{eq:stable-input-derivative-quotient}\n\\end{align}\nIn particular, \\(p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}\\) is strictly positive and smooth,\n\\(\\|\\nabla\\log p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}\\|_\\infty<\\infty\\), and\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:stable-input-translation-continuity}\n \\|\\partial^\\gamma p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\mathord\\cdot-z)\n       -\\partial^\\gamma p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}\\|_1\\longrightarrow0\n \\qquad(z\\to0).\n\\end{equation}\nIf the characteristic exponent is changed from \\(|\\xi|^\\alpha\\) to\n\\(a|\\xi|^\\alpha\\), put \\(\\lambda=a^{1/\\alpha}\\).  The new unit-scale density\nis \\(p_{1,a}(y)=\\lambda^{-d}p_1(y/\\lambda)\\).  Thus the density bound has\nfactor \\(\\lambda^{-d}\\), the derivative bound has factor\n\\(\\lambda^{-d-|\\gamma|}\\), and the quotient bound has factor\n\\(\\lambda^{-|\\gamma|}\\), with \\(1+|y|\\) replaced throughout by\n\\(1+|y|/\\lambda\\).  Equivalently, all later\nconstants are locally uniform when \\(a\\) ranges in a compact subset of\n\\((0,\\infty)\\).\n\\end{proposition}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nProperties (G)(i)--(iii) of \\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017}, also recorded\nin the refined formulation of\n\\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2022RefinedFractional}, give strict positivity,\nsmoothness, the derivative upper bounds, and the positive tail asymptotic\n\\(p_1(y)\\asymp |y|^{-d-\\alpha}\\) outside a sufficiently large ball.  The\ntail asymptotic supplies the lower bound in\n\\eqref{eq:stable-input-density} there.  On the remaining compact ball,\nstrict positivity and continuity give a positive minimum; enlarging the\nupper constant completes the global two-sided density bound.  Dividing\n\\eqref{eq:stable-input-derivative} by this lower bound proves\n\\eqref{eq:stable-input-derivative-quotient}, including the log-gradient\nbound.  The derivative estimate makes every \\(\\partial^\\gamma p_1\\)\nintegrable, so ordinary \\(L^1\\)-translation continuity gives\n\\eqref{eq:stable-input-translation-continuity}.  The assertions about \\(a\\)\nfollow directly by differentiating the displayed dilation formula.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Stable critical translation remainder]\n\\label{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder}\nLet \\(d\\ge1\\), \\(0<\\alpha<2\\), \\(p=p_{\\alpha,d}\\),\n\\(q=q_{\\alpha,d}\\), and \\(m=\\lfloor p\\rfloor\\).  If\n\\(T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(y,z)\\) is the Taylor polynomial of\n\\(F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)\\) at \\(z=0\\) through degree \\(m\\), then\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth}\n c_{\\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\\beta(q-1)}\n \\le \\|F_\\cdot^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)\\|_{L^q(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})}^q\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d,q}(1+|z|)^{\\beta(q-1)}.\n\\end{equation}\nMoreover,\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}\n \\|F_\\cdot^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\cdot,z)\\|_{L^q(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})}\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d}\n \\begin{cases}\n  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\\le1,\\\\\n  |z|^p,&|z|>1,\n \\end{cases}\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d}|z|^p.\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nProposition~\\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} supplies all density,\nderivative, quotient, and translation estimates used below.  The upper\nbound in \\eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} follows from\n\\[\n \\begin{aligned}\n \\int p_1(y-z)^q p_1(y)^{1-q}\\dd y\n &\\le C\\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\\beta q}\n              (1+|y|)^{\\beta(q-1)}\\dd y\\\\\n &\\le C(1+|z|)^{\\beta(q-1)}\n       \\int(1+|y-z|)^{-\\beta}\\dd y,\n \\end{aligned}\n\\]\nwhere \\(p_1=p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}\\) and\n\\(1+|y|\\le(1+|z|)(1+|y-z|)\\).  The final integral is finite because\n\\(\\beta>d\\).  For the lower bound, integrate over \\(|y-z|\\le1\\) and use\n\\eqref{eq:stable-input-density}; this gives the claimed power\nfor \\(|z|\\ge2\\).  Positivity and continuity on bounded \\(z\\)-sets complete\nthe estimate.\n\nFor \\(|z|\\le1\\), Proposition~\\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} also gives\n\\(p_1(y-\\theta z)\\le C p_1(y)\\), uniformly in \\(0\\le\\theta\\le1\\).\nTaylor\'s formula along the segment from \\(y\\) to \\(y-z\\), followed by the\nderivative bound in \\eqref{eq:stable-input-derivative}, therefore\ngives the pointwise bound\n\\(|F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(y,z)|\\le C|z|^{m+1}\\), uniformly\nin \\(y\\).  For \\(|z|>1\\), \\eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} gives\n\\(\\|F_\\cdot^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)\\|_q\\le C|z|^{\\beta(1-1/q)}\\).  The Taylor\ncoefficients are bounded, so\n\\(\\|T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\cdot,z)\\|_q\\le C|z|^m\\).  Finally,\n\\[\n \\beta(1-1/q)\\le p,\\qquad m\\le p<m+1,\n\\]\nwith equality in the first relation when \\(\\beta>4\\).  These observations\nprove \\eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder}.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Critical Bregman perturbation bound]\n\\label{lem:critical-lq-kl-perturbation}\nLet \\(1<q\\le2\\) and\n\\(\\Phi(s)=(1+s)\\log(1+s)-s\\) on \\([-1,\\infty)\\), with\n\\(0\\log0=0\\).  There is a constant \\(C_q\\) such that\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-bregman-pointwise-bound}\n 0\\le \\Phi(u+v)-\\Phi(u)-\\log(1+u)v\\le C_q|v|^q\n\\end{equation}\nwhenever \\(|u|\\le1/4\\) and \\(u+v\\ge-1\\).\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe lower bound is convexity.  If \\(|v|\\le1/2\\), the segment between\n\\(u\\) and \\(u+v\\) is contained in \\([-3/4,3/4]\\).  Since\n\\(\\Phi\'\'(s)=(1+s)^{-1}\\) there, Taylor\'s theorem gives an upper bound\n\\(C v^2\\le C|v|^q\\).  If \\(v<-1/2\\), the admissible pairs\n\\((u,v)\\) range over a compact set and \\(|v|^q\\ge2^{-q}\\); continuity at\n\\(u+v=-1\\) gives the result.  If \\(v>1/2\\), direct expansion of the left\nside shows that it is at most \\(C(1+v)\\log(1+v)+Cv\\), which is bounded by\n\\(C_qv^q\\).  These three regions prove\n\\eqref{eq:critical-bregman-pointwise-bound}.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{theorem}[Optimal uniform sufficient moment exponent for stable KL asymptotics]\n\\label{thm:high-dimensional-kl-moment-threshold}\nLet \\(d\\ge1\\), \\(0<\\alpha<2\\), and let \\(\\nu\\) be a probability law on\n\\(\\RR^d\\) with mean \\(\\bar\\gamma\\).  Put\n\\(X=\\gamma-\\bar\\gamma\\), and assume\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-kl-moment-hypothesis}\n \\EE|X|^{p_{\\alpha,d}}<\\infty,\n \\qquad\n p_{\\alpha,d}=\\max\\left\\{2,\n \\frac{4(d+\\alpha)}{d+\\alpha+4}\\right\\},\n\\end{equation}\nthen the covariance \\(\\Sigma=\\EE[XX^{\\mathsf T}]\\) is finite and\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-kl-leading-asymptotic}\n H_{\\alpha,d}(s):=\n D_{\\rm KL}\\!\\left(p_s^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\nu\\,\\middle\\|\\,\n p_s^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\mathord\\cdot-\\bar\\gamma)\\right)\n =\\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)s^{-4}+o(s^{-4}),\n\\end{equation}\nwhere\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:stable-leading-covariance-functional}\n b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}(y)\n :=\\frac1{2p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)}\n   \\sum_{i,j=1}^d\\Sigma_{ij}\\partial_{ij}p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y),\n \\qquad\n \\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)\n :=\\frac12\\int b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}^2\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}.\n\\end{equation}\nThe exponent is optimal only in the following uniform sense.  For every\n\\(0<r<2\\), there is a mean-zero law with finite \\(r\\)th absolute moment\nand \\(\\limsup_{s\\to\\infty}s^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s)=+\\infty\\).  If\n\\(d+\\alpha>4\\), then for every \\(2\\le r<p_{\\alpha,d}\\) the counterexample\nmay additionally be chosen with positive-definite finite covariance.\nThus no smaller moment exponent implies\n\\eqref{eq:critical-kl-leading-asymptotic} uniformly over its entire moment\nclass, and the endpoint belongs to the sufficient side.\n\nThis is not a law-by-law moment criterion.  When \\(d+\\alpha>4\\), finite\n\\(p_{\\alpha,d}\\)-moment is not asserted to be necessary for an individual\nlaw; the exact finite-covariance criterion is the nonlinear raw-tail energy\nin Theorem~\\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} below.  When\n\\(d+\\alpha\\le4\\), the exponent is two and boundedness of\n\\(s^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s)\\) does force finite covariance, as the proof below\nshows.  For \\(\\alpha=1\\) with the standard normalization\n\\(p_1^{(1,d)}=P_1^{(d)}\\), one has\n\\(\\mathcal Q_{1,d}=\\mathcal Q_d\\), so the theorem contains the radial\nPoisson result above.\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nTranslation permits us to assume \\(\\bar\\gamma=0\\).  Fix\n\\(q=q_{\\alpha,d}\\), \\(p=p_{\\alpha,d}\\), and \\(m=\\lfloor p\\rfloor\\),\nand write\n\\[\n R_m(y,z)=F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(y,z),\n \\qquad r_s(y)=\\EE R_m(y,X/s).\n\\]\nMinkowski\'s inequality and\n\\eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder} give\n\\[\n s^p\\|R_m(\\cdot,X/s)\\|_q\\le C_{\\alpha,d}|X|^p.\n\\]\nFor each fixed \\(X\\), the local part of the same estimate and \\(m+1>p\\)\ngive\n\\[\n s^p\\|R_m(\\cdot,X/s)\\|_q\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d}|X|^{m+1}s^{p-m-1}\\longrightarrow0.\n\\]\nDominated convergence therefore yields\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-lq-integrated-remainder}\n \\|r_s\\|_{L^q(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-p}).\n\\end{equation}\n\nCentering removes the linear Taylor layer.  Averaging the remaining layers\ngives\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-kl-quotient-decomposition}\n \\delta_s^{(\\alpha,d)}=u_s+r_s,\n \\qquad\n u_s=s^{-2}b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}\n       +\\mathbf 1_{\\{m=3\\}}s^{-3}B_3,\n\\end{equation}\nwhere \\(B_3\\) is a bounded linear combination of third-order modes.  In the\nsecond case the required third moments exist because \\(p\\ge3\\).  Hence\n\\(\\|u_s\\|_\\infty=O(s^{-2})\\).  The boundedness of all these modes follows\nfrom Proposition~\\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}.\n\nThe identity\n\\(F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}(\\dd y)\n=p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y-z)\\dd y\\) shows that every translated quotient has\nintegral one.  Moreover,\n\\(\\int|F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-1|\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}(\\dd y)\\le2\\), so Tonelli\'s\ntheorem gives \\(\\delta_s^{(\\alpha,d)}\\in L^1(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})\\) with\nzero integral.  The KL change of variables is therefore\n\\[\n H_{\\alpha,d}(s)=\\int\\Phi(\\delta_s^{(\\alpha,d)})\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\n\\]\nin the extended sense.  For all sufficiently large \\(s\\), apply\nLemma~\\ref{lem:critical-lq-kl-perturbation} to \\(u=u_s\\), \\(v=r_s\\).\nHölder\'s inequality and \\eqref{eq:critical-lq-integrated-remainder} give\n\\begin{align*}\n \\left|H_{\\alpha,d}(s)-\\int\\Phi(u_s)\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\\right|\n &\\le \\|\\log(1+u_s)\\|_{q/(q-1)}\\|r_s\\|_q\n       +C_q\\|r_s\\|_q^q\\\\\n &\\le O(s^{-2})o(s^{-p})+o(s^{-pq})=o(s^{-4}),\n\\end{align*}\nbecause \\(p\\ge2\\) and \\(pq=4\\).\nThis estimate also proves that the extended KL integral is finite for all\nsufficiently large \\(s\\).\n\nFinally, the boundedness of the retained modes permits a uniform Taylor\nexpansion of \\(\\Phi(u_s)\\).  From\n\\eqref{eq:critical-kl-quotient-decomposition},\n\\[\n \\int\\Phi(u_s)\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\n =\\frac{s^{-4}}2\\int b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}^2\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\n   +o(s^{-4})\n =\\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)s^{-4}+o(s^{-4}),\n\\]\nwhich proves \\eqref{eq:critical-kl-leading-asymptotic}.\n\nWe first prove the obstruction below two moments.  If\n\\(\\limsup_{s\\to\\infty}s^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s)<\\infty\\), Pinsker\'s inequality\nand scaling give, for every fixed \\(\\xi\\in\\RR^d\\),\n\\[\n |\\widehat p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\xi)|\n |\\varphi_X(\\xi/s)-1|\n \\le \\|p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\nu_s-p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}\\|_1\n \\le \\sqrt{2H_{\\alpha,d}(s)}=O(s^{-2}),\n\\]\nwhere \\(\\nu_s\\) is the law of \\(X/s\\).  Since the stable characteristic\nfunction never vanishes, take \\(\\xi=e\\) for a unit vector \\(e\\), multiply\nthe real part by \\(s^2\\), and use Fatou\'s lemma to obtain\n\\[\n \\frac12\\EE(e\\cdot X)^2\n \\le \\liminf_{s\\to\\infty}s^2\n       \\EE[1-\\cos((e\\cdot X)/s)]<\\infty.\n\\]\nThus bounded scaled entropy forces finite covariance.  Given \\(0<r<2\\),\nchoose \\(a\\in(\\max\\{1,r\\},2)\\) and put symmetric masses proportional to\n\\(n^{-a-1}\\) at \\(\\pm ne_1\\), with the remaining mass at zero.  This law\nhas mean zero and finite \\(r\\)th moment but infinite variance, so its scaled\nentropy has infinite limsup.\n\nIt remains to prove optimality between two and \\(p\\) when \\(\\beta>4\\).\nFix \\(2\\le r<p\\), choose positive \\(a_j\\) with \\(\\sum_ja_j<\\infty\\), and\nput symmetric masses \\(w_j/2\\) at \\(\\pm R_je_1\\), where\n\\(w_j=a_jR_j^{-r}\\).  Add a sufficiently small bounded symmetric spanning\ncomponent.  The resulting law has positive-definite finite covariance and\nfinite \\(r\\)th moment.  Set\n\\[\n s_j=\\kappa R_jw_j^{1/\\beta},\\qquad\n A_j=B(R_je_1,s_j).\n\\]\nThe component at \\(R_je_1\\) gives\n\\((p_{s_j}^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\nu)(A_j)\\ge c_{\\alpha,d}w_j\\).  On the other hand,\n\\eqref{eq:stable-input-density} and \\(s_j/R_j\\to0\\) give\n\\[\n p_{s_j}^{(\\alpha,d)}(A_j)\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d}(s_j/R_j)^\\beta\n =C_{\\alpha,d}\\kappa^\\beta w_j.\n\\]\nChoose \\(\\kappa\\) so that\n\\(C_{\\alpha,d}\\kappa^\\beta<c_{\\alpha,d}\\).  Data processing to\n\\(\\{A_j,A_j^c\\}\\) and\nLemma~\\ref{lem:bernoulli-kl-linear-separation} then yield\n\\(H_{\\alpha,d}(s_j)\\ge c w_j\\), and hence\n\\[\n s_j^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s_j)\n \\ge cR_j^4w_j^{1+4/\\beta}\n =ca_j^{q_{\\alpha,d}}R_j^{4-rq_{\\alpha,d}}.\n\\]\nHere \\(q_{\\alpha,d}=1+4/\\beta\\) and\n\\(r<p=4/q_{\\alpha,d}\\), so the exponent of \\(R_j\\) is positive.\nRecursive choice of the radii makes \\(s_j\\to\\infty\\) and the last display\nunbounded while preserving all moment assertions.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[All-order stable critical remainder]\n\\label{lem:all-order-stable-critical-remainder}\nLet \\(r\\ge1\\), put \\(\\beta=d+\\alpha\\), and define\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:all-order-stable-critical-exponents}\n q_{r,\\alpha,d}:=\\min\\left\\{2,1+\\frac{2r}{d+\\alpha}\\right\\},\n \\qquad\n p_{r,\\alpha,d}:=\\frac{2r}{q_{r,\\alpha,d}}\n =\\max\\left\\{r,\\frac{2r(d+\\alpha)}{d+\\alpha+2r}\\right\\}.\n\\end{equation}\nLet \\(q=q_{r,\\alpha,d}\\), \\(p=p_{r,\\alpha,d}\\), and\n\\(m=\\lfloor p\\rfloor\\).  If \\(T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(y,z)\\) is the Taylor\npolynomial of \\(F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)\\) at zero through degree \\(m\\), then\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder}\n \\|F_\\cdot^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\cdot,z)\\|_{L^q(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})}\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d,r}\n \\begin{cases}\n  |z|^{m+1},&|z|\\le1,\\\\\n  |z|^p,&|z|>1,\n \\end{cases}\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d,r}|z|^p.\n\\end{equation}\nConsequently, if a probability law \\(\\lambda\\) on \\(\\RR^d\\) has finite\n\\(p\\)th absolute moment and\n\\[\n q_s^\\lambda(y):=\\int F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(x/s)\\lambda(\\dd x),\n\\]\nthen\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:all-order-stable-integrated-remainder}\n q_s^\\lambda\n =1+\\sum_{j=1}^m s^{-j}B_j^\\lambda+r_s^\\lambda,\n \\qquad\n \\|r_s^\\lambda\\|_{L^q(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-p}),\n\\end{equation}\nwhere\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:all-order-stable-moment-modes}\n B_j^\\lambda(y):=\n \\frac{(-1)^j}{p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)}\n \\sum_{|\\gamma|=j}\\frac{m_\\gamma(\\lambda)}{\\gamma!}\n \\partial^\\gamma p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y),\n \\qquad\n m_\\gamma(\\lambda):=\\int x^\\gamma\\lambda(\\dd x).\n\\end{equation}\nEvery \\(B_j^\\lambda\\) in this display is bounded.\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe proof of \\eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} applies verbatim for\nevery fixed \\(1<q\\le2\\) and gives\n\\[\n \\|F_\\cdot^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)\\|_{L^q(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})}\n \\le C(1+|z|)^{\\beta(1-1/q)}.\n\\]\nThe local Taylor argument in the proof of\nLemma~\\ref{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder} gives the first line\nof \\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder}.  For \\(|z|>1\\), the\nTaylor modes are bounded by\nProposition~\\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}, and\nhence\n\\[\n \\|F_\\cdot^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\cdot,z)\\|_q\n \\le C\\{|z|^{\\beta(1-1/q)}+|z|^m\\}\\le C|z|^p.\n\\]\nIndeed, \\(m\\le p\\), while\n\\(\\beta(1-1/q)\\le p\\); in the non-Hilbert regime\n\\(\\beta>2r\\), both sides of the latter inequality equal\n\\(2r\\beta/(\\beta+2r)\\).  Since \\(m+1>p\\), the final inequality in\n\\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder} also holds on the unit ball.\n\nTaylor\'s formula gives \\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-integrated-remainder}\nbefore its norm assertion.  For fixed \\(x\\), the local estimate implies\n\\[\n s^p\\|F_\\cdot^{(\\alpha,d)}(x/s)\n       -T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\cdot,x/s)\\|_q\\longrightarrow0,\n\\]\nwhereas \\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder} bounds this expression\nby \\(C|x|^p\\).  Minkowski\'s inequality and dominated convergence prove the\nclaimed \\(L^q\\) remainder.  Boundedness of the modes follows again from\nProposition~\\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Two-background critical Bregman transfer]\n\\label{lem:two-background-critical-bregman-transfer}\nLet \\(1<q\\le2\\), \\(p\\ge r>0\\), and \\(pq=2r\\).  On a probability space\n\\((E,\\Omega)\\), suppose \\(g_s\\ge c_s>0\\),\n\\[\n \\int g_s\\dd\\Omega=1,\\qquad c_s\\longrightarrow1,\n \\qquad \\|g_s-1\\|_{L^1(\\Omega)}\\longrightarrow0.\n\\]\nLet \\(B\\in L^\\infty(\\Omega)\\), and suppose\n\\[\n v_s=s^{-r}B+o(s^{-r})\\quad\\hbox{in }L^\\infty(\\Omega),\n \\qquad \\|e_s\\|_{L^q(\\Omega)}=o(s^{-p}).\n\\]\nIf \\(g_s+v_s+e_s\\ge0\\) and both \\(g_s\\Omega\\) and\n\\((g_s+v_s+e_s)\\Omega\\) are probability measures, then\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:two-background-critical-bregman-transfer}\n D_{\\rm KL}((g_s+v_s+e_s)\\Omega\\|g_s\\Omega)\n =\\frac{s^{-2r}}2\\int B^2\\dd\\Omega+o(s^{-2r}).\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{lemma}\n\nThe hypotheses on the denominator in this lemma deliberately stop short of\n\\(L^\\infty\\)-convergence to one. +from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import unittest
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+
+
+class CompanionArticleTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_article_has_required_branches(self) -> None:
+        main = (ROOT / "main.tex").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        for source in (
+            "sec_entropy_asymptotics",
+            "sec_verified_A2_results",
+            "sec_entropy_30_eighth_defect_layer",
+            "sec_gram_space",
+            "sec_strip_00_poisson_image",
+            "sec_strip_10_hardy_aux_lattice",
+            "sec_strip_20_symbol_sampling",
+            "sec_strip_30_cardinal_observation",
+        ):
+            self.assertIn(rf"\input{{{source}}}", main)
+
+    def test_no_printed_relocation_proof_path_is_active(self) -> None:
+        main = (ROOT / "main.tex").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        self.assertNotIn("relocatedproof", main)
+        self.assertNotIn("Supplementary Material", main)
+
+    def test_bibliography_matches_citations(self) -> None:
+        aux = (ROOT / "main.aux").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        bibliography = (ROOT / "bibliography_companion.tex").read_text(
+            encoding="utf-8"
+        )
+        cited = set(re.findall(r"\\citation\{([^}]+)\}", aux))
+        items = set(re.findall(r"\\bibitem\{([^}]+)\}", bibliography))
+        self.assertEqual(cited, items)
+
+    def test_metadata_records_unassessed_status(self) -> None:
+        metadata = (ROOT / "submission_metadata.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        self.assertIn("separated from", metadata)
+        self.assertIn("No venue assessment has yet been made", metadata)
+        self.assertIn("No target journal or acceptance probability", metadata)
+
+    def test_numbering_is_automatic_and_sources_fit_limit(self) -> None:
+        active = "\n".join(
+            path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for path in ROOT.glob("*.tex")
+        )
+        self.assertNotRegex(active, r"\\tag\s*\{")
+        self.assertNotRegex(active, r"\\setcounter\s*\{")
+        for path in ROOT.glob("*.tex"):
+            self.assertLess(len(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()), 800)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+\title[Cauchy--Poisson Coefficients and Sampling]{Cauchy--Poisson Entropy
+Coefficients, Gaussian Quadrature, and Lattice Observation}
+\author{Anonymous author}
+\date{}
+
+\keywords{Cauchy convolution, Poisson kernel, relative entropy asymptotics,
+Cayley transform, Gaussian quadrature, reproducing kernel Hilbert space,
+integer-lattice sampling}
+\subjclass[2020]{42A38, 46E22, 60E10, 94A17}
+
+\begin{document}
+\begin{abstract}
+We develop an exact coefficient calculus for the relative entropy of a
+one-dimensional law after large-scale Cauchy smoothing.  The Cayley transform
+turns normalized Poisson translates into finite Laurent modes and identifies
+the pullback reference measure with Haar measure.  This yields an all-order
+even expansion, a finite Fourier algorithm for its coefficients, and sharp
+moment thresholds for their canonical evaluation.  In particular, finite
+variance is equivalent to bounded fourth-order scaled relative entropy, and
+the sixth- and eighth-order coefficient defects admit explicit positive
+decompositions and rigidity statements.
+
+Moment matching links the coefficient hierarchy to Gaussian quadrature.  For
+an \(n\)-node quadrature law, the first unmatched moment determines the
+leading relative-entropy coefficient; the missing-moment boundary and
+regularly varying alternatives are treated separately.  We also prove an
+exact nonlocal Bregman tail identity for the moving Cauchy comparison and
+Poisson-specific raw-tail decompositions that retain the nonlinear part not
+captured by a finite moment jet.
+
+The same Cayley modes generate a reproducing kernel Hilbert space.  We
+identify its Poisson image, compute the integer-orbit symbol, and prove the
+associated cardinal projection and observation-channel sampling theorem.
+Integer samples recover exactly the lattice projection; full recovery holds
+precisely on the corresponding lattice subspace.  Thus the coefficient,
+quadrature, and sampling results are organized by a single observation
+mechanism: Cauchy smoothing compactifies the law into Fourier data whose
+finite jets control entropy and whose full mode profile supports Hilbert-space
+reconstruction.
+\end{abstract}

+\begin{lemma}[Uniform Bernoulli relative-entropy separation]
+\label{lem:bernoulli-kl-linear-separation}
+Let \(0<b<a\).  If \(u\ge aw\) and \(v\le bw\) are Bernoulli parameters,
+then
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(\operatorname{Ber}(u)\|\operatorname{Ber}(v))
+ \ge a\left\{\log\frac ab-1+\frac ba\right\}w.
+\]
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+If \(v=0<u\), the relative entropy is infinite.  Otherwise \(u>v>0\), and
+\[
+ (1-u)\log\frac{1-u}{1-v}\ge-(u-v).
+\]
+Writing \(\vartheta=v/u\le b/a<1\) gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(\operatorname{Ber}(u)\|\operatorname{Ber}(v))
+ \ge u\{\log(1/\vartheta)-1+\vartheta\}
+ \ge aw\left\{\log\frac ab-1+\frac ba\right\},
+\]
+because the braced function is decreasing on \((0,1)\).
+\end{proof}

+\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
+
+Let
+\[
+ P_t(x)=\frac1\pi\frac{t}{t^2+x^2},\qquad t>0,
+\]
+be the one-dimensional Poisson, or Cauchy, kernel.  For a probability law
+\(\nu\) with centre \(\bar\gamma\), we study the large-scale relative
+entropy
+\[
+ H_\nu(t)=D_{\rm KL}(P_t*\nu\|P_t(\mathord\cdot-\bar\gamma)).
+\]
+The normalized translate quotient is rational, and the Cayley coordinate
+\[
+ z=\frac{x-\ii t}{x+\ii t}
+\]
+maps the real line to the unit circle while sending the Cauchy reference to
+Haar measure.  Consequently the Taylor modes of the quotient become finite
+Laurent polynomials.  This elementary compactification is the common source
+of the three parts of the paper.
+
+First, it gives a finite coefficient calculus for \(H_\nu(t)\).  The density
+quotient has an all-order expansion whose modes are polynomial functions of
+the centred moments of \(\nu\); Haar integration reduces every entropy
+coefficient to a constant Laurent term.  Parity removes the odd powers.  The
+result is an explicit even expansion
+\[
+ H_\nu(t)=\sum_{m=2}^{N}A_{2m}(\nu)t^{-2m}+o(t^{-2N})
+\]
+under the stated finite-moment hypotheses, together with a finite Fourier
+algorithm for each \(A_{2m}\).  The coefficient domain is sharp: canonical
+finiteness of \(A_{2m}\) is equivalent to the precise centred absolute
+moment required by its top Cayley mode.  At the leading order, finite
+variance is equivalent to boundedness of \(t^4H_\nu(t)\), including the
+converse for arbitrary laws rather than only those admitting a Taylor
+expansion.
+
+Second, moment matching converts the same expansion into a quadrature
+statement.  If two laws agree below the first unmatched order, the leading
+relative entropy is the squared norm of that unmatched mode.  Applied to an
+\(n\)-node Gaussian quadrature law, exactness below degree \(2n\) identifies
+the first missing moment with the squared \(L^2(\nu)\)-norm of the monic
+orthogonal polynomial.  We treat finite and missing top moments separately;
+the latter cannot be inferred from a formal coefficient substitution.  The
+critical regularly varying boundary illustrates why vague tail data alone
+does not determine a nonlinear entropy limit.
+
+The coefficient identities also produce higher defect formulas.  The sixth-
+and eighth-order coefficients admit decompositions in orthogonal polynomial
+coordinates, yielding a two-level defect ladder, amplification, and
+two-point rigidity.  These statements retain their original moment
+hypotheses: the seventh-moment bridge used for an eighth-order remainder is
+not replaced by a purely algebraic calculation.
+
+Third, the complete Cayley mode family carries more information than any
+finite coefficient jet.  Its Gram kernel defines a Hilbert completion, and
+the Poisson image realizes that completion as a strip RKHS.  Integer
+translates generate a lattice subspace with an explicitly computable symbol.
+The associated cardinal operator reconstructs the orthogonal lattice
+projection from integer observation samples.  Full recovery is therefore a
+subspace statement, not a claim that arbitrary laws are determined by a
+finite or lattice-restricted entropy jet.
+
+The moving Cauchy comparison supplies a dynamic counterpart to the static
+coefficient calculus.  We prove the nonlocal Bregman identity with complete
+domain and endpoint closure and derive its coefficient consequences.  A
+Poisson raw-tail decomposition then separates the universal covariance mode
+from the nonlinear energy carried beyond the smoothing scale.  This tail
+description and the quadrature boundary results explain where a finite mode
+jet ceases to control the full entropy.
+
+\subsection*{Main results and organization}
+
+Sections~2 and~3 establish the Cayley--Haar normalization and the Poisson
+quotient calculus.  Section~4 proves the moving-quotient Bregman identity and
+its endpoint representation.  Section~5 develops moment matching, Gaussian
+quadrature, and the sharp dimensional entropy thresholds.  Section~6 gives
+the higher coefficient defects and stability statements.  Section~7 records
+the Poisson raw-tail consequences.  Sections~8 and~9 construct the mode RKHS,
+its strip realization, and the integer-lattice observation theorem.
+
+The paper uses Gaussian quadrature only as an exact algebraic moment-matching
+device; numerical integration is not part of any proof.  Likewise, the
+sampling theorem recovers the lattice projection, with full reconstruction
+only under membership in the lattice subspace.  These scope boundaries are
+part of the theorem statements rather than additional claims of the article.

+\begin{proof}
+For finitely supported \(c\), the Toeplitz identity and Parseval give
+\[
+ \|Cc\|_{\mathcal H}^2
+ =\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}
+   \sigma(\theta)|\widetilde c(\theta)|^2\dd\theta.
+\]
+The bounds on \(\sigma\) prove the Riesz inequalities and extend \(C\) to
+an isomorphism from \(\ell^2\) onto its closed range.  By the definition of
+\(V\), this range is \(V\).  The discrete Fourier transform diagonalizes
+\(G\) as multiplication by \(\sigma\), so \(G\) is invertible and
+\(G^{-1}\) is multiplication by \(\sigma^{-1}\).  The identity
+\(R(Cc)=Gc\), first on a dense set and then by continuity, shows that
+\(R=GC^{-1}\) on \(V\); hence \(R\) is an isomorphism and
+\(R^{-1}=CG^{-1}\).
+
+If \(G^{-1}\alpha=d\), then
+\(\widetilde d=\widetilde\alpha/\sigma\).  A second application of the
+norm identity gives
+\[
+ \|R^{-1}\alpha\|_{\mathcal H}^2
+ =\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}
+ \sigma\left|\frac{\widetilde\alpha}{\sigma}\right|^2\dd\theta
+ =\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}
+ \frac{|\widetilde\alpha|^2}{\sigma}\dd\theta.
+\]
+Taking \(\alpha=\delta_0\) proves the cardinal assertion.
+\end{proof}

+# Submission Metadata
+
+## Article
+
+- Title: *Cauchy--Poisson Entropy Coefficients, Gaussian Quadrature, and Lattice Observation*
+- Author line: Anonymous author
+- Primary source: `main.tex`
+
+## Provenance
+
+This article was separated from *Stable-Flow Relative Entropy Dissipation and
+Optimal Stable-Kernel Moment Exponents* during the structural reconstitution
+of that article.  It contains the Cauchy coefficient hierarchy,
+Gaussian-quadrature consequences, higher coefficient defects, RKHS
+completion, and integer-lattice sampling results that no longer belong to the
+stable-flow article.
+
+The material has been assembled here as one paper because the Cayley--Poisson
+observation mechanism links its coefficient, quadrature, Hilbert-space, and
+sampling components.  No venue assessment has yet been made for this paper.
+No target journal or acceptance probability is recorded.

 \begin{document}
-\def\JFAArticleMain{1}
 \begin{abstract}
-For two probability measures with finite \((d+\alpha)\)-th absolute moments,
-we prove a relative-entropy dissipation theorem for their simultaneous
-symmetric \(\alpha\)-stable heat flows.  On every positive compact time
-window the density quotient is bounded above and below and has bounded
-logarithmic gradient; the associated logarithmic nonlocal Dirichlet form is
-finite, locally integrable, and equals the negative entropy derivative.  An
-annular argument closes the two noncompact Green pairings separately, and a
-Wasserstein bound closes the endpoint at infinity, giving an exact
-tail-integral representation.  The two-solution entropy-production identity
-and its one-sided Bregman algebra are classical.  Our contribution is the
-stable-continuum measure-data domain and endpoint theorem for that identity.
-With a stable moving reference, we provide an exact nonlocal Bregman integral
-representation along Johnson's symmetric-stable interpolation, under the
-stated finite-moment and finite-initial-entropy domain; no identification
-with Johnson's score-pairing integrand is claimed.
+Let two probability measures evolve simultaneously under a symmetric
+\(\alpha\)-stable heat semigroup.  Under finite \((d+\alpha)\)-moments, we
+prove that their relative entropy is locally absolutely continuous and that
+its derivative is the negative logarithmic nonlocal Bregman form.  The result
+includes finiteness and local integrability of the dissipation, closure of the
+two noncompact Green pairings generated by the singular jump kernel, decay at
+infinity, and the endpoint representation of relative entropy as the tail
+integral of its dissipation.  A moving stable reference yields the analogous
+exact Bregman representation along the symmetric-stable interpolation.
 
-Arbitrary-order first unmatched moment relative-entropy asymptotics under
-Gaussian smoothing are due to Chen and Niles-Weed
-\cite{ChenNilesWeed2022SmoothedWasserstein}, while all-order
-stable/fractional heat-kernel density expansions are also prior work
-\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017,
-IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2022RefinedFractional}.  Neither result is claimed as
-new.  For the heavy-tailed isotropic strictly \(\alpha\)-stable kernels,
-\(0<\alpha<2\), we identify the optimal complete-moment condition that
-transfers the density expansion through relative entropy.
-If two
-laws on \(\RR^d\) match all tensor moments below the integer order \(r\ge1\),
-have a nonzero order-\(r\) difference \(\Delta_r\), and have finite
-\(p_{r,\alpha,d}\)th absolute moments, where
+For laws whose tensor moments agree below an integer order \(r\ge1\), we
+identify the optimal uniform complete-moment exponent
 \[
  p_{r,\alpha,d}=\max\left\{r,
- \frac{2r(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+2r}\right\},
+ \frac{2r(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+2r}\right\}.
 \]
-then
-\[
- D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
- =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
-\]
-The coefficient is an orthogonally invariant positive-definite quadratic
